title: Constraints on Horndeski Gravity with Phantom Crossing
comment: 21 pages, 11 figures. Submitted to MNRAS. Comments welcome
summary: Gravity models in which the dark energy equation of state crosses $w=-1$, also known as the phantom divide, have received extensive interest due to recent analyses favouring this behaviour. We introduce a new subclass of Horndeski scalar-tensor models capable of generating phantom crossing, whilst remaining minimally coupled to matter: the Asymptotic Cubic Galileon (ACG) models. We show that ACG models can jointly fit the expansion history inferred from observations of the Planck cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, and distance-ladder supernovae measurements from the Dark Energy Survey. We then demonstrate that perturbative observables, including the galaxy-ISW cross-correlation and void force profile, provide powerful constraints that confine viable and testable ACG models to a well-defined region of the broader Horndeski landscape. Model comparison metrics, including $χ^{2}$ and Bayesian evidence, favour both ACG and $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM models over $Λ$CDM, with ACG providing a fit of comparable quality to $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM. Crucially, ACG models ground the observationally preferred $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM behaviour in a robust Lagrangian formulation. This enables interpretation beyond mere phenomenological fits, and motivates further tests of these models on nonlinear scales.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Asymptotic Cubic Galileon models that enable dark energy equation of state to cross w=-1, fit current cosmological data well, and offer a robust theoretical basis that outperforms ΛCDM, motivating deeper testing in cosmology.
AI.motivation: To address recent observational analyses favoring dark energy equation of state crossing the phantom divide (w=-1) and to provide a robust theoretical framework for such behavior.
AI.method: Introduction of a new subclass of Horndeski scalar-tensor models named Asymptotic Cubic Galileon (ACG) models, minimally coupled to matter, and analyzing their fit to cosmological expansion history and perturbative observables.
AI.result: ACG models successfully fit Planck CMB, BAO, and supernova data; perturbative observables tightly constrain viable ACG models within the Horndeski parameter space; model comparison metrics favor ACG and w0waCDM over ΛCDM, with ACG offering comparable fit and a firm theoretical foundation.
AI.conclusion: The ACG subclass provides a theoretically grounded model consistent with observationally preferred phantom crossing behavior, enabling interpretation beyond phenomenological fits and motivating further testing at nonlinear scales.

title: Raising the reionization optical depth with inflationary CMB features
summary: Within the highly successful $Λ$CDM paradigm established with cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropy measurements, the optical depth through reionization $τ$ is the most uncertain due both to the difficulty in measuring large-angle polarization and the assumptions made in their interpretation. Currently, for the Planck primary data in the flat $Λ$CDM cosmology with slow-roll inflation and standard reionization, the one-sided 95% upper limit for $τ$ is $τ_{\rm max}=0.0696$. Yet when all current CMB measurements excluding large-angle polarization are combined with baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements, the one-sided 95% lower limit is an incompatible $τ_{\rm min}=0.074$. If the long-standing low-power feature of the temperature measurements is interpreted as physically originating from inflation then $τ$ inferred from large-angle polarization becomes larger. Marginalizing over templates of the low-power feature based on the generalized slow-roll formalism of inflation raises the Planck maximum to a more compatible $τ_{\rm max}=0.075$ which further increases to $τ_{\rm max} = 0.082$ with the inclusion of all CMB+BAO data. This marginalization does not assess the statistical significance of the low-power feature itself; rather, it shows that allowing a higher $τ$ is a consequence of interpreting the anomaly as a physical feature instead of a statistical fluctuation.

AI.tldr: The paper resolves discrepancies in the measurement of the optical depth τ in ΛCDM cosmology by interpreting low-power temperature anomalies as inflationary features, raising τ's upper limit and reconciling CMB polarization data with other cosmological probes.
AI.motivation: To address the uncertainty in the optical depth through reionization (τ) measurements within the ΛCDM model, particularly reconciling discrepancies between large-angle polarization data and other cosmological observations.
AI.method: Data analysis combining Planck primary CMB data, excluding large-angle polarization, with baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements, and marginalizing over low-power feature templates based on the generalized slow-roll inflation formalism to reinterpret anomalies in temperature measurements.
AI.result: Marginalizing over low-power inflation feature templates raises the upper limit of τ, reconciling it with lower limits from combined CMB+BAO data. This adjustment reflects interpreting the temperature anomaly as a physical inflationary feature rather than a statistical artifact, increasing the maximum τ estimate from 0.0696 to 0.082.
AI.conclusion: Allowing τ to be higher by marginalizing over inflation-based low-power feature templates resolves the tension between CMB large-angle polarization and other cosmological measurements, indicating that the anomaly's interpretation critically affects τ estimates within the ΛCDM framework.

title: Euclid: Quick Data Release (Q1) -- LensMC shear measurement catalogue for cluster lensing science
summary: We present a LensMC lensing analysis of Euclid Quick Release 1 images that were made available in March 2025. We measured shapes, positions, weights, and other morphological parameters of galaxies with a surface number density of $26\;\text{arcmin}^{-2}$ for $I_{\scriptscriptstyle\rm E}<24.5$, achieving 75 arcmin$^{-2}$ for $I_{\scriptscriptstyle\rm E}<27$, in 63 deg$^2$ of Euclid VIS images. This is the first shear measurement catalogue produced with \lensmc in anticipation of the Euclid Data Release 1. To within the scope of this work and availability of survey volume, we found no spatial dependency in the additive biases. However, we developed an empirical bias correction based jointly on galaxy sizes and magnitudes, which was applied to the measurement of the lensing signal over the whole area. In order to validate the quality of our measurements, we calculated two-point statistics and cluster profile measurements, and cross-checked results with external cluster catalogues from WISE and the Dark Energy Survey. Additionally, by stacking shear profiles of random clusters we found that the low-redshift, large radii bins may be still contaminated by residual systematic effects. Thanks to Euclid image resolution and depth and overall good control of systematic errors, we are able to constrain the lensing profiles of clusters with masses of $10^{14}M_\odot$ out to $z\approx2$ over nearly 10 Gyr of evolution history.

AI.tldr: This study presents the first LensMC shear catalogue from Euclid Quick Release 1 images, applies bias corrections, validates measurements with statistical and external catalogue comparisons, and constrains cluster lensing profiles up to redshift 2, demonstrating high-quality lensing analysis with controlled systematics.
AI.motivation: To analyze and validate the shear measurements from Euclid Quick Release 1 images for weak lensing studies, focusing on systematic bias correction and enabling cluster lensing profile constraints over a wide redshift range.
AI.method: Used LensMC for lensing analysis on Euclid VIS images, measuring galaxy shapes and morphologies, applying empirical bias corrections based on galaxy size and magnitude, and validating results with two-point statistics and comparisons to external cluster catalogues (WISE, DES).
AI.result: Produced the first LensMC shear measurement catalogue for Euclid DR1, with no detected spatial additive bias dependencies; confirmed measurement quality through statistical tests and cross-checks, identifying some residual systematics at low redshift and large radii, and constrained cluster lensing profiles up to redshift ~2.
AI.conclusion: The analysis demonstrates that Euclid Quick Release 1 data, combined with LensMC and empirical bias corrections, provide reliable shear measurements with controlled systematics, enabling precise cluster lensing studies over a significant redshift span and cosmic time.

title: Loss-Cone-Limited Dark Matter Accretion onto Early Black Hole Seeds
summary: The rapid appearance of supermassive black holes at high redshift motivates a reassessment of non-baryonic growth channels. We develop a loss-cone framework for collisionless dark-matter (DM) capture by early black-hole seeds, with particular attention to phase-space depletion and refilling. The calculation combines Eddington-inverted NFW-like halos, a relativistic direct-capture boundary, and an orbit-averaged Fokker-Planck treatment of angular-momentum transport. Primordial black holes (PBHs) are treated as massive perturbers whose refilling strength depends on both their abundance and individual mass. Collisionless refilling by triaxial or chaotic centrophilic orbits is included as a phenomenological upper-envelope channel. We show that ordinary stellar relaxation gives negligible DM-driven growth for the fiducial high-redshift seeds. PBH-driven granularity can yield order-of-magnitude growth in sufficiently compact halos, while triaxial or full-loss-cone supply can produce a rapid early burst. In the self-consistent calculations, however, the evolution generally becomes supply-limited. Once the accessible low-angular-momentum phase-space reservoir is depleted, the capture rate collapses and the black-hole mass saturates. Fixed-background NFW calculations therefore overestimate sustained growth, especially in the full-loss-cone limit. A TNG50-calibrated NFW benchmark gives negligible growth even under optimistic refilling assumptions. Collisionless DM capture is therefore unlikely to solve early SMBH growth in generic NFW-like halos, but it can provide a radiatively dark upper envelope in rare compact environments with efficient angular-momentum refilling.

AI.tldr: This study models collisionless dark matter capture by early black-hole seeds and finds that while mechanisms like primordial black holes and triaxial orbits can boost growth, phase-space depletion limits sustained accretion, making this channel insufficient to explain early supermassive black hole growth in typical halos.
AI.motivation: The rapid emergence of supermassive black holes at high redshift challenges existing growth models and motivates exploration of non-baryonic dark matter accretion mechanisms.
AI.method: Developed a loss-cone framework incorporating Eddington-inverted NFW-like halos, relativistic capture boundaries, orbit-averaged Fokker-Planck angular momentum transport, and PBHs as perturbers, with additional phenomenological modeling of collisionless refilling channels.
AI.result: Found that stellar relaxation contributes negligibly to DM-driven growth; PBHs and triaxial orbits can enhance growth but are ultimately limited by phase-space depletion; fixed-background NFW models overestimate growth; TNG50-calibrated models predict negligible growth.
AI.conclusion: Collisionless dark matter capture alone is insufficient to explain early supermassive black hole growth in typical NFW-like halos, though it may contribute in rare, compact halos with efficient angular momentum refilling.

title: Old and Bright: The Remarkable Radio Brightening of the Engine-driven SN 2012au Several Years After Explosion Signals the Birth of a PWN
comment: 39 pages, 20 figures, 4 tables, Submitted to ApJ
summary: We present the results from an extensive broad-band (radio to X-rays) observing campaign of the engine-driven Type Ib SN 2012au in the first 13 years of evolution. The early-time ($δt\leq{190}$ d) radio and X-ray evolution is well-described by conventional models of a forward shock interacting with a wind-like circumstellar medium ($ρ_{\rm{CSM}}\propto{r}^{-2}$). However, starting at $δ{t}\approx{6.7}$ yr, we detect a significant radio re-brightening. This late-time emission is dominated by a luminous component characterized by a broad and rapidly evolving spectral peak and a shallow optically thin spectral slope, $F_ν\proptoν^{-0.31\pm0.02}$. These properties imply a compact emitting region ($R\lesssim{10}^{16}$ cm) expanding at a remarkably slow velocity ($\lesssim{500}$ km/s) into a high-density environment ($\geq{10}^4 \rm{cm}^{-3}$), accompanied by a hard electron power-law index $p\approx{1.6}$. No soft or hard X-ray emission is detected at any epoch, indicating that high-energy radiation is either strongly absorbed or intrinsically absent. In the context of aspherical shock-CSM interaction models, these observations imply extreme properties of the CSM (geometry, density, total mass) that lack clear astrophysical motivation. Instead, we show that the emergence of radiation from a newborn Pulsar Wind Nebula (PWN) naturally explains the radio spectral evolution and high-energy limits, where the emission is governed by the adiabatic expansion of a relic pair plasma. We conclude that SN 2012au represents the most compelling candidate for a young, newborn PWN discovered to date, a scenario that can be directly tested with pending Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observations.

AI.tldr: Extensive multi-wavelength monitoring of SN 2012au reveals early shock-CSM interaction followed by a late-time radio re-brightening best explained by a newborn Pulsar Wind Nebula, making SN 2012au a prime candidate for a young PWN.
AI.motivation: To understand the late-time radio re-brightening and spectral evolution observed in the Type Ib SN 2012au over 13 years.
AI.method: Extensive broad-band observational campaign from radio to X-rays, analyzing early and late-time emission and comparing results with shock-CSM interaction models and PWN emission scenarios.
AI.result: Early-time data fit conventional shock-CSM models; late-time re-brightening shows a compact region with slow expansion and hard electron index, no X-ray detection. The observations favor a newborn Pulsar Wind Nebula (PWN) origin over aspherical shock-CSM interaction.
AI.conclusion: SN 2012au likely harbors a young, newborn PWN which naturally explains the radio spectral evolution and high-energy non-detections, providing the most compelling candidate for such an object so far, testable with future VLBI observations.

title: Accurate Galaxy Cluster Shear and Mass Calibration for LSST with AnaCal
summary: The observed abundance of galaxy clusters as a function of mass and redshift provides a powerful route to precision cosmology; a key challenge for cluster cosmology is to establish the relation between cluster observables and cluster masses, for which cluster weak gravitational lensing has become the standard tool. A key challenge for cluster lensing is that the shear signal near cluster centers can reach the non-linear regime, where many shear estimators rely on perturbative assumptions that must be explicitly validated. In this work, we use image simulations to test the performance of the shear estimator AnaCal for cluster weak lensing under conditions representative of the 10-year LSST data. We find that AnaCal recovers the input shear with minimal bias even at mildly high shear, $|g|\sim 0.15$. We discover a radially decreasing mean shear response as seen previously in data, driven by the radial dependence of the convergence field; if unmodeled, this effect can bias shear inference. We also find a positive shear-estimation bias at third order in the reduced shear near the cluster center. However, because only a small fraction of galaxies lie in the high-shear regime and those measurements are further downweighted by the covariance matrix, the resulting mean cluster-mass bias for cluster lens masses in $[10^{14} M_\odot, 10^{15} M_\odot]$ -- adopting a scale cut of $\sim 0.2$ Mpc at $z=0.25$ -- is $0.24 \pm 0.26\%$ under ideal settings. These results demonstrate that AnaCal is a robust tool for accurate cluster mass calibration in the LSST era.

AI.tldr: This paper validates the AnaCal shear estimator using LSST-like image simulations, demonstrating minimal bias in cluster weak lensing measurements critical for precise cluster mass calibration in cosmology.
AI.motivation: Establishing the accurate relation between cluster observables and cluster masses for precision cosmology, particularly addressing challenges in shear estimation for weak gravitational lensing near cluster centers.
AI.method: Use of image simulations to test the performance of the AnaCal shear estimator under conditions representative of 10-year LSST data, focusing on analyzing shear recovery, shear response, and bias effects near cluster centers.
AI.result: AnaCal recovers input shear with minimal bias even at mildly high shear values; detects a radially decreasing mean shear response driven by convergence field that can bias inference if unmodeled; observes a positive third-order shear estimation bias near cluster centers; overall mean cluster-mass bias is negligible (0.24 ± 0.26%) for cluster masses in the range [10^14, 10^15] solar masses with appropriate scale cuts.
AI.conclusion: AnaCal is validated as a robust and accurate shear estimator tool for cluster mass calibration suitable for data from the LSST era, capable of controlling shear estimation biases that could affect cluster cosmology analyses.

title: Radio Follow Up of a Sub-threshold GRB in the Sky Localization Area of GW241125
summary: Since the Fermi satellite's identification of a candidate $γ$-ray burst (GRB) temporally coincident with GW150914, several tentative, and often debated, associations between electromagnetic (EM) transients and gravitational-wave (GW) signals from binary black hole (BBH) mergers have been reported. One such event, S241125n (later confirmed as GW241125_010116), was identified during the fourth observing run (O4) of Advanced LIGO and found to be spatially (within large GW localization uncertainty) and temporally coincident with a subthreshold GRB detected by the Swift Burst Alert Telescope Gamma-ray Urgent Archiver for Novel Opportunities (BAT-GUANO). Here, we present results from a radio follow-up campaign targeting the BAT-GUANO localization region, carried out with the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA). We also re-analyze Swift/XRT observations of the field, and combine these results with optical upper limits. Our analysis constrains the isotropic kinetic energy of a putative relativistic jet launched in the BBH merger to $\lesssim 3 \times 10^{50}$ erg for $n_{ISM} = 1.0 cm^{-3}$. We also discuss both the challenges and the diagnostic power of radio follow up in assessing candidate BBH-GRB associations, and present projections for analogous radio studies in the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run 5 (O5), and in the era of next-generation ground-based instrumentation. The enhanced sensitivity and localization capabilities of detector networks such as Cosmic Explorer and the Einstein Telescope, paired with the enhanced sensitivity of next-generation radio interferometers such as the next-generation VLA and the Square Kilometre Array, will significantly strengthen coordinated multi-messenger follow-up of BBHs. These next-generation facilities are likely to provide an answer to whether BBHs host relativistic ejecta powered by mini-disk accretion.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes radio and X-ray follow-ups of a candidate GRB associated with a BBH merger, constraining jet energy and discussing future prospects for multi-messenger observations with advanced detectors and radio telescopes.
AI.motivation: To investigate possible electromagnetic counterparts to binary black hole (BBH) mergers, focusing on the candidate GRB associated with the GW event GW241125_010116.
AI.method: Conducting radio follow-up observations using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA), re-analyzing Swift/XRT data, and incorporating optical upper limits to constrain the kinetic energy of any relativistic jets from the BBH merger.
AI.result: The isotropic kinetic energy of a hypothetical relativistic jet in the BBH merger is constrained to be less than approximately 3 x 10^{50} erg for an interstellar medium density of 1 cm^{-3}. The study highlights the challenges of radio follow-up in confirming BBH-GRB associations and projects improvements with next-generation observatories.
AI.conclusion: Current radio observations set strong limits on relativistic jets from BBH mergers like GW241125_010116, but future detector networks (Cosmic Explorer, Einstein Telescope) and enhanced radio arrays (next-generation VLA, SKA) will greatly improve multi-messenger follow-up capabilities, potentially resolving whether BBHs produce relativistic ejecta from mini-disk accretion.

title: Are Cosmological Data Excluding Sterile Neutrinos or Only the Fully Thermalized Limit?
comment: 22 pages, 6 figures, and 6 tables. Comments are welcome
summary: We present a cosmological reassessment of light sterile-neutrino scenarios, examining whether current observations exclude sterile neutrinos as a class or primarily constrain the fully thermalized case. We consider three distinct realizations: (i) a fully thermalized sterile species (FTS), (ii) a thermal relic with a suppressed temperature relative to the active neutrino background (DTS), and (iii) a Dodelson-Widrow-like (DW) sterile neutrino with reduced phase-space normalization. Constraints are derived within both LambdaCDM and the CPL dynamical dark-energy framework using combinations of Planck CMB data, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and the PantheonPlus and Union3 Type Ia supernova samples. For baseline data combinations without a local H0 prior, the FTS scenario is strongly disfavored in both cosmological models. Adding the local H0^DN prior allows LambdaCDM+FTS to accommodate the high local H0 value and become statistically competitive with standard LambdaCDM once SNIa data are included, although the sterile-neutrino mass remains consistent with zero. By contrast, partially populated sterile-neutrino scenarios remain viable: the DW realization is broadly compatible with current observations, while the DTS scenario yields the weakest cosmological pressure among the cases considered. Overall, cosmological data mainly require a strongly suppressed effective sterile abundance, leading to tight constraints on m_eff^sterile while allowing substantially weaker bounds on the physical sterile mass. We conclude that current observations do not generically exclude sterile neutrinos, but rather place strong pressure on fully thermalized or highly populated scenarios, highlighting the importance of production history and phase-space distribution when interpreting cosmological constraints.

AI.tldr: The study reexamines sterile neutrino cosmology with current data, finding that fully thermalized sterile neutrinos are strongly constrained, while partially populated scenarios remain viable. Cosmological limits mainly suppress effective abundance rather than physical mass, emphasizing the role of sterile neutrino production and phase-space distribution in cosmological models.
AI.motivation: To reassess the cosmological viability of light sterile neutrino scenarios under current observational constraints, distinguishing between fully thermalized and partially populated cases.
AI.method: Analyzing cosmological data combinations including Planck CMB, DESI BAO, and Type Ia supernovae within LambdaCDM and CPL dynamical dark-energy models to constrain three sterile neutrino realizations: fully thermalized (FTS), suppressed-temperature thermal relic (DTS), and Dodelson-Widrow-like (DW).
AI.result: Fully thermalized sterile neutrinos are strongly disfavored unless a local H0 prior is included, which relaxes constraints somewhat; partially populated scenarios (DW and DTS) remain compatible with data, with DTS facing the weakest cosmological pressure. Strong limits exist on effective sterile abundance and mass, but physical sterile neutrino mass bounds are weaker.
AI.conclusion: Current cosmological observations do not exclude the presence of sterile neutrinos generically but strongly constrain scenarios with full thermalization or high population. The production history and distribution of sterile neutrinos critically affect the interpretation of cosmological constraints.

title: Little Red Dots as Supermassive Analogs of SS 433
summary: High-redshift little red dots (LRDs) are compact sources characterized by V-shaped spectral energy distributions (SEDs), broad emission lines, and often prominent Balmer breaks. Their high number density and apparently large black hole masses suggest that they are essential to the early evolution of galaxies and supermassive black holes (SMBHs); however, the nature of their central engines remains uncertain. Here, we propose that LRDs are the supermassive, high-redshift analogs of the hyper-Eddington accreting Galactic microquasar SS~433, viewed at high inclinations. By scaling the hyper-Eddington accretion physics from stellar-mass black holes to supermassive scales, we show that the observed LRD features, including X-ray weakness, soft optical SEDs, apparent sub-Eddington accretion ratio, and Balmer breaks, emerge naturally from the self-shielding geometry of a puffed-up accretion disk. In this framework, the broad-line regions are ionized by anisotropic radiation escaping from the inner disk, analogous to the unseen UV/X-ray emission revealed by the W50 nebula in SS 433. Their low-inclination or lower-accretion-rate counterparts would appear as little blue dots (LBDs) or normal active galactic nuclei. Our model predicts that the Balmer break strength positively correlates with the broad-line width, that the emission lines are more variable than the optical continuum, that LRDs are intrinsically more luminous than observed, and that LBDs are more variable than LRDs. This unified-scale model redefines LRDs as the essential laboratories for observing the rapid accretion-driven growth that shaped the early assembly of galaxies and their central SMBHs.

AI.tldr: The paper models high-redshift little red dots as supermassive analogs of SS 433 with hyper-Eddington accretion, explaining their unique spectral features and variability, and highlights their importance in studying early black hole and galaxy growth.
AI.motivation: The study aims to understand the nature of high-redshift little red dots (LRDs), which are compact sources with unique spectral features and significant implications for early galaxy and SMBH evolution, but whose central engines are not well understood.
AI.method: The authors propose a model that scales hyper-Eddington accretion physics from stellar-mass black holes to supermassive black holes, interpreting LRDs as high-inclination views of supermassive analogs to the Galactic microquasar SS 433. They analyze observed LRD properties within a self-shielding, puffed-up accretion disk geometry.
AI.result: The model explains observed LRD characteristics including X-ray weakness, soft optical SEDs, sub-Eddington accretion ratios, and Balmer breaks as natural outcomes of the proposed geometry. It predicts correlations between Balmer break strength and emission line width, greater variability in emission lines than in optical continuum, intrinsic luminosities higher than observed, and distinct variability patterns for LRDs and their low-inclination counterparts (LBDs).
AI.conclusion: LRDs are best understood as supermassive, hyper-Eddington accreting black holes viewed at high inclination angles, analogous to SS 433 scaled up, making them critical laboratories for observing rapid early SMBH growth and galaxy assembly.

title: Wave-optics imprints of dark matter subhalos on strongly lensed gravitational waves. II. Saddle images and detectability
summary: Wave-optics interference in strongly lensed gravitational waves is a new interferometric probe of dark matter substructure: a subhalo population threading a galaxy-scale lens imprints frequency-dependent distortions on the amplification factor of each macro image. In a companion paper (arXiv:2603.04267), we computed these imprints for the magnified minimum image. Here, we extend the calculation to the saddle-point image and we assess the detectability of the combined signal with the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). Evaluating the amplification factor at a saddle is numerically delicate, because the equal-arrival-time contours are open and the subhalo signal is a small difference of large terms; we present a time-domain method that resolves it. Across a Monte Carlo ensemble of cold dark matter subhalo realizations, subhalos induce percent-level amplitude and phase modulations in both image parities, while the mean (de)magnification splits by parity: the minimum is net magnified and the saddle net demagnified. Demodulating the macro-image interference recovers the per-image modulations, and a matched-filter analysis that projects out the lens parameters yields a combined detection above $5σ$ in $62\%$ of realizations for fiducial massive-black-hole-binary sources of total mass $\sim10^{6}\,M_\odot$ at redshift $1.5$, provided the source lies close to the lens caustic at small impact parameter $y_{\rm src}\lesssim0.1$. Folding these naive per-event significances through optimistic strong-lensing rate forecasts yields $10$-$20$ substructure detections over the LISA mission. Strongly lensed gravitational waves are thus a sensitive, complementary probe of substructure at $10^{4}$-$10^{7}\,M_\odot$ scales inaccessible to electromagnetic observations.

AI.tldr: This paper extends wave-optics interference analysis of strongly lensed gravitational waves to saddle-point images, develops a time-domain numerical method, and demonstrates that LISA can detect dark matter subhalos through characteristic modulations in gravitational wave signals, predicting 10-20 detections over the mission lifetime.
AI.motivation: To utilize wave-optics interference in strongly lensed gravitational waves as a novel interferometric probe of dark matter substructure, specifically to detect subhalos that affect the lensing amplification factor.
AI.method: Extended previous calculations of frequency-dependent distortions in the amplification factor from the magnified minimum image to the saddle-point image; developed a time-domain numerical method to evaluate amplification factors at saddle points; conducted Monte Carlo simulations of cold dark matter subhalo realizations; performed matched-filter analyses to project out lens parameters and assess detectability with LISA.
AI.result: Subhalos induce percent-level amplitude and phase modulations in both minimum and saddle images, with distinct net magnification/demagnification by parity; combined signal detection above 5σ achieved in 62% of realizations for typical massive-black-hole binary sources near lens caustics; projected 10-20 substructure detections during the LISA mission based on strong-lensing rate forecasts.
AI.conclusion: Strongly lensed gravitational waves provide a sensitive and complementary probe of dark matter substructure at mass scales (10^4 - 10^7 solar masses) that are otherwise inaccessible through electromagnetic observations.

title: XRISM Time-resolved Fe K$α$ Spectroscopy of NGC 4395: Time-variable Inner-disk Emission
comment: 16 pages, 11 figures, accepted for publication in the ApJL
summary: We report the first XRISM observation of the low-mass AGN in the nearby dwarf galaxy NGC 4395 ($M_{\rm BH}\sim10^{4-5}\,M_\odot$), complemented by a simultaneous NuSTAR observation. We constrained the continuum by jointly fitting the XRISM/Resolve (2-12 keV) and NuSTAR (3-30 keV) spectra while excluding the Fe K band (5.5-7.5 keV). Relative to this baseline continuum, the time-averaged Resolve spectrum revealed an unresolved neutral Fe K$α$ core with a velocity width of $\lesssim$110 km s$^{-1}$ and an adjacent redward wing. The red wing was well reproduced by an additional relativistically broadened Fe K component. Furthermore, time-resolved spectroscopy with $\approx$87 ks bins showed that the diskline profile varied significantly over the $\sim$400 ks observation. This evolution can be interpreted in terms of changes in the inner radius of the line-emitting region, together with a possible inclination modulation with a period of $\approx$210 ks. If interpreted as Lense-Thirring precession of a tilted inner flow, the observed period would favor the low end of the black hole mass estimates ($M_{\rm BH}\approx9\times10^3\,M_\odot$) and imply a moderate spin ($a\gtrsim0.6$). These results highlight the capability of XRISM to track relativistic disk dynamics in AGNs.

AI.tldr: First XRISM plus NuSTAR observations of NGC 4395 reveal relativistic Fe K line variability consistent with Lense-Thirring precession, enabling black hole mass and spin estimates in a low-mass AGN.
AI.motivation: To investigate the low-mass AGN in the dwarf galaxy NGC 4395 using high-energy X-ray observations to understand relativistic disk dynamics.
AI.method: Joint spectral fitting of XRISM/Resolve (2-12 keV) and NuSTAR (3-30 keV) data excluding the Fe K band, complemented by time-resolved spectroscopy with 87 ks bins over a 400 ks observation.
AI.result: Detection of an unresolved neutral Fe Kα core with a narrow velocity width and a redward relativistically broadened Fe K component; observed variability in diskline profile interpreted as changes in inner radius and possible inclination modulation with a ~210 ks period, consistent with Lense-Thirring precession and implying a black hole mass near 9×10^3 M⊙ and moderate spin (a≳0.6).
AI.conclusion: XRISM can effectively track relativistic disk dynamics in AGNs, providing constraints on black hole mass and spin through time-resolved spectroscopy of relativistically broadened Fe K features.

title: Dark Energy in the DESI Era: A Brief Review of Evidence, Beyond-$Λ$CDM Interpretations, and Tensions
comment: 29 pages, 12 figures; Invited Review for RAA (Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics), prepared for the Special Forum: "Dark Energy and the Hubble Constant Crisis" at the 28th Annual Conference of the China Association for Science and Technology
summary: Recent baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from DESI provide important new clues for reassessing whether the standard $Λ$CDM model offers a sufficient description of the late-time expansion history of the Universe. When combined with cosmic microwave background and type Ia supernova data, these measurements show an apparent departure from the $Λ$CDM model, commonly described as dynamical dark energy (DDE) with equation of state crossing the phantom divide (i.e., quintom behavior). This review examines the current status of the DESI-motivated indications for DDE and their possible implications for physics beyond $Λ$CDM. We discuss how the strength of the preference for DDE depends on the adopted parametrization and dataset combination, and how residual systematics or internal tensions among datasets may affect its interpretation. At the background level, several mechanisms beyond $Λ$CDM can produce similar expansion histories. We therefore further discuss how the same effective departure from $w=-1$ may arise from physically distinct scenarios, including interacting dark energy, non-minimally coupled gravity, and non-standard dark matter. Meanwhile, these different new-physics interpretations may have different implications for current cosmological tensions, especially those involving $H_0$, $S_8$, and $\sum m_ν$. In conclusion, the question posed by DESI is not merely whether dark energy evolves with time, but rather how, within the framework of precision cosmology, to disentangle new physics scenarios from systematic errors.

AI.tldr: DESI baryon acoustic oscillation data challenge the standard $\Lambda$CDM model by suggesting time-evolving dark energy. This review discusses how different models and dataset choices affect this interpretation and the need to disentangle new physics from observational systematics.
AI.motivation: Recent baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from DESI suggest potential deviations from the standard $\Lambda$CDM model, prompting a reassessment of whether this model adequately describes the Universe's late-time expansion.
AI.method: The paper reviews the current status of DESI-motivated evidence for dynamical dark energy (DDE), analyzing various parametrizations and dataset combinations, and discussing the interpretation challenges posed by residual systematics and internal dataset tensions. It also explores alternative physical models beyond $\Lambda$CDM that can mimic similar expansion histories.
AI.result: The review identifies indications of DDE with quintom behavior but notes that these results depend strongly on the choice of parametrization and datasets. It highlights multiple new-physics scenarios (interacting dark energy, non-minimally coupled gravity, non-standard dark matter) that could explain the effective departure from $w=-1$, each with distinct implications for current cosmological tensions such as $H_0$, $S_8$, and neutrino mass sum.
AI.conclusion: The critical issue raised by DESI data is not only whether dark energy evolves over time but how to distinguish genuine new physics from systematic errors within precision cosmology frameworks.

title: Probing dipole and quadrupole anisotropy in Gamma-ray bursts from Swift dataset
comment: 18 pages, 17 figures. Accepted for publication in Universe
summary: Testing the validity of the cosmological principle's assumption of large-scale isotropy remains crucial for modern cosmology. We investigate the angular distributions of gamma-ray bursts using the GRB catalog from Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory (Swift) for an independent probe of isotropy. Using the HEALPix spherical harmonic decomposition, we estimate the dipole and quadrupole amplitudes and compare them against the null hypothesis obtained from 500 isotropic Monte Carlo realizations. Our results show 2.9$σ$ dipole and 7.2$σ$ quadrupole amplitude when applied to the raw data. To account for observational biases, we then create an exposure map using the pointing history, roll angle, and the partial coding fraction of the Swift Telescope. Reevaluating the null hypothesis using this map reduces the significance of these anisotropies to less than $1σ$. Therefore, our findings confirm statistical isotropy of the GRB sky using the Swift data, consistent with previous studies. We have also made the Swift exposure map publicly available.

AI.tldr: By analyzing Swift gamma-ray burst data and accounting for observational biases via a detailed exposure map, the study finds no statistically significant large-scale anisotropy in the GRB sky, confirming cosmological isotropy.
AI.motivation: To test the validity of the cosmological principle's assumption of large-scale isotropy through an independent astrophysical probe.
AI.method: Analyzed the angular distribution of gamma-ray bursts from the Swift GRB catalog using HEALPix spherical harmonic decomposition to estimate dipole and quadrupole amplitudes, compared against isotropic Monte Carlo simulations; subsequently accounted for observational biases by creating an exposure map based on Swift telescope's pointing history, roll angle, and partial coding fraction.
AI.result: Initial analysis showed significant dipole and quadrupole amplitudes (2.9σ and 7.2σ respectively), but after correcting for observational biases with the exposure map, significance dropped below 1σ, indicating consistency with statistical isotropy.
AI.conclusion: The study confirms the statistical isotropy of the GRB sky based on Swift data, validating the cosmological principle assumption of isotropy at large scales; the publicly available exposure map facilitates further research in this area.

title: Optimization of Tessellation-based Statistics: Void Statistics
summary: Tessellation methods are extensively employed in the analyses of cosmic large-scale structure (LSS). However, these techniques are highly sensitive to perturbations in both densities and positions of points, often leading to substantial rearrangements of tessellation configurations. As a result, considerable additional statistical errors are introduced in various tessellation-based statistics, thereby weakening their cosmological constraints. In this work, we identify this issue and propose an efficacious measurement scheme through subsampling and averaging to enhance the stabilities of tessellation-based statistics. As a case study, we apply the new scheme to measure multiple primary void statistics [i.e., void size function (VSF), void two-point correlation function (VTCF), and void power spectrum (VPS)] in two distinct classes of voids, based on Delaunay and Voronoi tessellations, respectively. We notice that the statistical uncertainties in void statistics can be predominantly attributed to tessellation instabilities. Through rigorous testing, we demonstrate that the proposed method can substantially eliminate these scatters to deeply mine the statistical power of void statistics. Specifically, we find that our method can dramatically boost the signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) of void Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAOs) and significantly improve the constraining power of void statistics on cosmological parameters. These findings showcase enormous application potentials of our new method in maximizing extraction of cosmological information from galaxy surveys. Importantly, our method is simple yet highly potent with broad applicability, hopefully evolving into a standard framework for measuring tessellation-based statistics in the future.

AI.tldr: A new subsampling and averaging method robustly stabilizes tessellation-based cosmic void statistics, greatly increasing their precision and cosmological constraint power.
AI.motivation: Tessellation-based analyses of cosmic large-scale structure are highly sensitive to perturbations, leading to statistical errors that weaken cosmological constraints.
AI.method: Introduced a subsampling and averaging scheme to stabilize tessellation-based statistics, applied specifically to void size function, void two-point correlation function, and void power spectrum on Delaunay and Voronoi tessellations.
AI.result: The method substantially reduces statistical instabilities, dramatically boosts signal-to-noise ratios of void Baryon Acoustic Oscillations, and significantly enhances cosmological parameter constraints.
AI.conclusion: The proposed subsampling and averaging approach effectively mitigates tessellation instabilities, improving the robustness and cosmological utility of void statistics from galaxy surveys, with broad applicability and potential to become a standard framework.

title: A broadband view of the thermal and non-thermal emission from the embedded massive star cluster RCW 38
comment: Submitted to A&A. Comments are welcome
summary: Gamma-ray emission has now been detected from a variety of source classes in the Galaxy, including clusters of young massive stars. RCW 38, a very young embedded massive star cluster, is a case of particular interest: its gamma-ray emission detected up to hundreds of GeV, provided the first observational evidence of high-energy particle acceleration powered exclusively by stellar winds. In this work, we aim to characterize the emission mechanisms responsible for the gamma-ray flux in RCW 38 and to provide estimates of the acceleration efficiency, as well as the fraction of accelerated electrons compared to protons, $K_{ep}$. We present the most comprehensive multi-wavelength study of a single star cluster to date. Our analysis ranges from MHz radio observations obtained with the GLEAM-X survey from the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) to GeV gamma-ray data from Fermi-LAT, and includes GHz and THz measurements from Parkes, Planck, and IRAS. We model the thermal and non-thermal emission of RCW 38 using an eight-parameter model constrained by the Markov chain Monte Carlo method. Our results support an interpretation in which the gamma-ray emission from RCW 38 is produced by hadronic interactions with the host molecular cloud. We derive robust constraints on the electron-to-proton ratio, with $K_{ep} \lesssim 10^{-3}$, and on the acceleration efficiency, estimated to be $\gtrsim$1%, consistent with the values required to explain the cosmic-ray composition, and in particular its $^{22}$Ne anomaly. These results strengthen the idea that stellar clusters play a significant role as contributors to cosmic-ray protons in our Galaxy at least up to energies of a few TeV. Future investigations with the next generation of ground-based detectors will determine whether they also play a relevant role at higher energies, particularly in the context of the cosmic-ray knee.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a multi-wavelength analysis of gamma-ray emission from the young star cluster RCW 38, demonstrating hadronic origins of the emission, constraining particle acceleration parameters, and reinforcing stellar clusters as important cosmic-ray proton sources in the Galaxy.
AI.motivation: To understand the mechanisms behind gamma-ray emission from the young star cluster RCW 38, a unique case showing high-energy particle acceleration powered solely by stellar winds.
AI.method: A comprehensive multi-wavelength study combining MHz radio data from GLEAM-X/MWA, GeV gamma-ray data from Fermi-LAT, and GHz to THz data from Parkes, Planck, and IRAS. The thermal and non-thermal emissions were modeled using an eight-parameter framework constrained via Markov chain Monte Carlo methods.
AI.result: The gamma-ray emission is primarily produced by hadronic interactions with the host molecular cloud. Constraints on the electron-to-proton ratio were found to be $K_{ep} \\lesssim 10^{-3}$, and acceleration efficiency is estimated at $\\gtrsim$1%, consistent with cosmic-ray composition requirements, particularly the $^{22}$Ne anomaly.
AI.conclusion: Stellar clusters like RCW 38 significantly contribute to cosmic-ray protons in the Galaxy up to a few TeV in energy, supporting their role in Galactic cosmic-ray sources. Future ground-based detectors will clarify their impact at higher energies, near the cosmic-ray knee.

title: Phantom-Divide Crossing in Exponentially Coupled Quintessence and the Role of Neutrino-Mass Freedom
summary: We investigate a quintessence dark-energy model with an exponential potential and an exponential coupling to cold dark matter (CDM), hereafter referred to as the CQ-EXP model, using Planck CMB, DESI BAO, and DES-Dovekie supernova observations. We also examine how variations in the neutrino mass sector affect the constraints. When the neutrino mass sum is fixed at $\sum m_ν=0.06$ eV, the data favor a coupling between quintessence and CDM, with the coupling parameter $β$ deviating from zero at more than $3σ$. In particular, the observations favor the $β<0$ branch, where the energy transfer between the two dark sectors changes sign and the effective equation of state (EoS) of dark energy crosses the phantom divide, $w=-1$. When the effective neutrino mass parameter $\sum m_{ν,\mathrm{eff}}$ is treated as a free parameter, the data show a preference for negative values of $\sum m_{ν,\mathrm{eff}}$. This additional freedom weakens the preference for the coupling between quintessence and CDM and leads to nearly identical values of $χ^2_{\rm min}$ for the CQ-EXP models with $β>0$ and $β<0$, corresponding respectively to models without and with phantom-divide crossing in the effective EoS. Both values are slightly larger than that obtained in the $w_0w_a$CDM model, indicating that the CQ-EXP model cannot be statistically distinguished from the $w_0w_a$CDM model with the data considered here. Therefore, when $\sum m_ν$ is fixed, current observations favor the CQ-EXP model with phantom-divide crossing. In contrast, when negative values of $\sum m_{ν,\mathrm{eff}}$ are allowed, a CQ-EXP dark energy without crossing $w=-1$ can also provide an effective explanation of the latest observations.

AI.tldr: The study analyzes a quintessence dark energy model coupled to cold dark matter using cosmological data, finding that fixed neutrino mass favors coupling with phantom-divide crossing in the dark energy equation of state, while variable neutrino mass weakens this preference and yields models statistically similar to standard cosmology.
AI.motivation: To explore the constraints on a quintessence dark-energy model with exponential potential and coupling to cold dark matter using the latest cosmological observations, including the impact of neutrino mass variations.
AI.method: Analyzing cosmological data from Planck CMB, DESI BAO, and DES-Dovekie supernova observations, examining the CQ-EXP model with fixed and free neutrino mass parameters, and assessing statistical preference for model parameters.
AI.result: With fixed neutrino mass sum (0.06 eV), data favor coupling between quintessence and CDM, particularly negative coupling leading to phantom-divide crossing in the dark energy equation of state. Allowing effective neutrino mass to vary weakens this preference and makes models with and without phantom-divide crossing statistically indistinguishable. Both CQ-EXP versions have slightly worse fits than the standard w0waCDM model.
AI.conclusion: Current cosmological observations suggest the CQ-EXP dark energy model with phantom-divide crossing when neutrino mass is fixed, but allowing variation in effective neutrino mass weakens this preference, making non-phantom models equally viable and statistically indistinguishable from standard models; thus, neutrino mass treatment critically influences constraints on dark energy-dark matter coupling.

title: A New Scaling of Neutron Star Tidal Deformability for Directly Probing the Core Equation of State
summary: The dimensionless tidal deformability, $Λ$, of neutron stars (NSs), inferred from gravitational-wave (GW) observations, has thus far been used primarily to constrain the pressure of dense matter near twice nuclear saturation density, leaving the core equation of state (EOS) largely inaccessible to inspiral-phase GW observations. We show that the core EOS can be probed directly through $Λ$ using a perturbative analysis of the dimensionless stellar-structure and tidal-response equations formulated in terms of scaled intrinsic variables, without invoking any specific EOS model. We uncover a remarkable EOS-insensitive scaling relation between $Λ$ and the central EOS parameter $\mathrm{X}\equiv P_{\rm c}/\varepsilon_{\rm c}$, where $P_{\rm c}$ and $\varepsilon_{\rm c}$ denote the central pressure and energy density, respectively. The relation is validated against a broad ensemble of physically viable EOSs. Applying it to tidal deformabilities inferred from events such as GW170817 enables a direct determination of $\mathrm{X}$. We further derive a tight lower bound, $Λ_{\rm{TOV}}\gtrsim 9.2^{+1.2}_{-1.2}$, for maximum-mass NSs along stable mass-radius sequences, quantitatively demonstrating that even the most compact stable NSs remain distinctly separated from black holes, for which $Λ_{\rm{BH}}=0$. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized connection between inspiral-phase tidal deformability and the core EOS, establishing a direct link between GW observables and the microphysics of ultradense matter in the strong-gravity regime. The resulting scaling establishes inspiral-phase tidal deformability as a direct and largely model-insensitive probe of the EOS of NS cores.

AI.tldr: A novel, model-insensitive scaling relation connects neutron star tidal deformability from gravitational waves to core EOS parameters, enabling direct probing of ultradense matter in neutron star cores and distinguishing them from black holes.
AI.motivation: Current gravitational-wave observations use neutron star tidal deformability to constrain the EOS near twice nuclear saturation density, but the dense core EOS remains largely inaccessible.
AI.method: A perturbative analysis of dimensionless stellar-structure and tidal-response equations is performed using scaled intrinsic variables, without assuming any specific EOS model, to directly relate dimensionless tidal deformability to the core EOS parameter.
AI.result: An EOS-insensitive scaling relation between the tidal deformability Λ and central EOS parameter X = Pc/εc is discovered and validated across diverse EOSs. Applying this relation to GW data enables direct determination of X. Additionally, a robust lower bound on Λ for maximum-mass neutron stars is derived, distinguishing them clearly from black holes.
AI.conclusion: Inspiral-phase tidal deformability provides a direct, largely model-independent probe of the neutron star core EOS, linking gravitational-wave observables to the microphysics of ultradense matter under strong gravity.

title: Dark Matter as an Inflationary Relic in Warm Inflation
summary: Warm inflation is usually expected to completely deplete the inflaton condensate by dissipating its energy into radiation. We show that this expectation fails in a simple and observationally viable regime. In a strongly dissipative warm inflationary scenario, the dissipative ratio, $Q=Υ/(3H)$, can fall rapidly after the end of inflation as the system approaches radiation domination, thereby suppressing further energy transfer to the thermal bath. This leads to a residual inflaton condensate, which subsequently evolves as an effectively non-dissipative scalar field. For potentials with a stable quadratic minimum, this remnant inflaton manifests as a cold dark matter component. We establish this mechanism for the minimal renormalizable potential, with a dissipative coefficient $Υ\propto T^3$. In this case, current cosmological data allow strong dissipation while leaving the inflaton mass weakly constrained by inflationary observables. The observed dark matter abundance then fixes its mass to be $m \approx 0.02\,{\rm MeV}$, while larger masses overclose the Universe. The transition to matter-like scaling occurs well before BBN, avoiding a long-lived inflaton dark radiation component. Relic inflaton dark matter therefore turns the post-inflationary dynamics of warm inflation into a new late time constraint on its parameter space.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that in strongly dissipative warm inflation, the inflaton condensate is not fully depleted but becomes cold dark matter, fixing the inflaton mass and providing new constraints on inflation models based on dark matter abundance and cosmological data.
AI.motivation: Warm inflation typically depletes the inflaton condensate into radiation, but this understanding might be incomplete in certain regimes; investigating whether a residual inflaton condensate can persist impacts dark matter models and cosmology.
AI.method: Analyzing a strongly dissipative warm inflation scenario with a dissipative coefficient proportional to temperature cubed, exploring how the dissipative ratio Q evolves post-inflation and the dynamics of the inflaton field in this regime, focusing on potentials with a stable quadratic minimum.
AI.result: The dissipative ratio Q decreases rapidly after inflation ends, suppressing energy transfer to radiation and resulting in a residual inflaton condensate behaving as a cold dark matter component. The inflaton mass is fixed by dark matter abundance at approximately 0.02 MeV, consistent with cosmological data, and this transition occurs before BBN, avoiding unwanted relics.
AI.conclusion: Contrary to common expectations, warm inflation can leave a remnant inflaton condensate that acts as cold dark matter, imposing new constraints on warm inflation parameter space and linking post-inflationary dynamics to late-time cosmological constraints.

title: The Fundamental Planes of Black Hole Activity for High-Synchrotron-Peaked BL Lacertae Objects
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 2 table, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: The radio--X-ray correlation and Fundamental Plane (FP) of black hole activity can serve as a diagnostic tool for the origin of X-ray emissions. There was a scaling relation between radio and X-ray emissions for High-synchrotron-peaked BL Lacertae objects (HBLs), i.e., $L_{\rm{R}}\propto L_{\rm{X}}^{0.64}$, which can be explained by ADAF-dominated mode or synchrotron cooling (Syn-c). However, many results of studying blazar physics show that the X-ray emissions of HBLs are mainly produced by the synchrotron process of jets. Therefore, Syn-c appears to provide a plausible explanation for this relation. To further clarify the origin of X-ray emissions of HBLs, we constructed a sample containing 69 HBLs in this paper to re-investigate their radio--X-ray correlation and FP. Considering the Doppler beaming effect, we find that the intrinsic radio--X-ray correlation and FP of HBLs are $L_{\rm R,int}\propto L_{\rm X,int}^{0.68}$ and $\log L_{\rm R,int}=(0.57\pm0.06)\log L_{\rm X,int}+(0.33\pm0.11)\log M_{\rm BH}+(12.65\pm2.00)$, respectively. Our results agree with the scaling relation mention above, which suggests these scaling relations are not artificial. By employing the theoretical model of Syn-c, we find that these shallow radio--X-ray correlations and FP are caused by Syn-c, which implies that the X-ray emissions of HBLs may be produced by rapidly cooling, high-energy electrons accelerated at a shock. This is consistent with results of the recent X-ray polarization observations of HBLs. Our results provide the observational evidence of $L_{\rm R}\propto L_{\rm X_{\text{Syn-c}}}^{0.6\sim0.7}$.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that the X-ray emissions in High-synchrotron-peaked BL Lacertae objects originate from synchrotron cooling of high-energy electrons, supported by intrinsic radio--X-ray correlations and the Fundamental Plane analysis adjusted for Doppler beaming.
AI.motivation: Previous studies showed a scaling relation between radio and X-ray emissions in HBLs that could be explained by ADAF or synchrotron cooling, but X-ray emissions were thought to be mainly from synchrotron jets, necessitating further clarification.
AI.method: Constructed a sample of 69 HBLs and re-investigated their radio--X-ray correlation and Fundamental Plane considering Doppler beaming effects; employed the theoretical model of synchrotron cooling (Syn-c).
AI.result: Found intrinsic radio--X-ray correlation $L_{R,int} \propto L_{X,int}^{0.68}$ and FP relation with black hole mass; results match previous scaling relations; concluded that Syn-c explains the shallow correlations and implies X-ray emission arises from rapidly cooling high-energy electrons accelerated at shocks, supported by X-ray polarization observations.
AI.conclusion: Intrinsic radio--X-ray correlations and the Fundamental Plane in HBLs are governed by synchrotron cooling mechanisms, confirming X-ray emissions originate from jet synchrotron processes involving rapidly cooling high-energy electrons.

title: The local ultraviolet signature of Type Ia supernova environments from HST and MUSE
summary: (Abridged.) The local environment of a Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) encodes information on progenitor age, star formation, dust, and chemical enrichment that may influence both its light-curve properties and its standardized luminosity. We assemble a homogeneous explosion-site dataset to test how near-ultraviolet (UV) imaging combined with optical integral-field spectroscopy improves the characterization of SN Ia environments and their connection to SN observables. We analyze 340 low-redshift SN Ia sites observed with HST/WFC3 F275W and matched VLT/MUSE spectroscopy. For each site we measure local photometry, extract a 1 kpc-aperture spectrum, model the stellar continuum with a joint UV+optical fit, derive local stellar and gas-phase properties, and fit the SN light curves with SALT3-NIR. UV emission is detected at 235 of the 337 sites with valid HST imaging. The UV- and Halpha-based SFR surface densities are strongly correlated, with the UV estimates systematically higher by about 0.5 dex. Including the UV constraint shifts local luminosity-weighted ages toward older values by a median of +0.20 dex for UV detections and +0.45 dex for UV non-detections, showing that UV data help break age-dust-metallicity degeneracies. Consistently, F275W-r is very strongly correlated with the joint-fit stellar age. Within the 169-SN Ia calibration sample, the joint stellar age, the Halpha specific SFR, and the UV specific SFR all correlate strongly with the SALT3 stretch parameter x1, with significances above 6.8 sigma. After standardization, Hubble-residual trends are weaker, with amplitudes of about 0.04-0.06 mag. The results support a primary age-stretch mechanism largely absorbed by standard light-curve corrections, while any residual luminosity dependence on local environment is weaker and subtler.

AI.tldr: Combining near-UV imaging with optical spectroscopy helps better characterize SN Ia environments, revealing that local stellar age primarily influences light-curve stretch, while residual luminosity dependence on environment after standardization is minor.
AI.motivation: To improve the characterization of Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) environments using combined near-ultraviolet (UV) imaging and optical integral-field spectroscopy, exploring how local environmental properties relate to SN light-curve features and standardized luminosity.
AI.method: Analyzed 340 low-redshift SN Ia sites with HST/WFC3 F275W UV imaging and VLT/MUSE optical spectroscopy; measured local photometry, extracted 1 kpc aperture spectra, modeled stellar continuum with joint UV+optical fits, derived local stellar and gas-phase properties, and fitted SN light curves with SALT3-NIR.
AI.result: UV emission was detected in 235 sites; UV-based star formation rate (SFR) surface densities correlated with Halpha estimates but were systematically higher; UV data shifted local stellar age estimates older, breaking age-dust-metallicity degeneracies. Strong correlations were found between stellar age, specific SFRs, and the SALT3 stretch parameter x1. After standardization, residual luminosity trends with environment were weak (~0.04-0.06 mag).
AI.conclusion: Incorporating UV imaging improves constraints on local stellar population ages and star formation, clarifying the primary age-related mechanism influencing SN Ia light-curve stretch. Standard light-curve corrections mitigate much of the environmental dependence on luminosity, leaving only subtle residual effects.

title: Subgrid Modelling for Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics with Machine Learning
summary: Resolving the impact of magnetic field instabilities in triggering small scale turbulent flow and the associated rearrangement of the field is of critical importance in understanding multimessenger observables in binary neutron star mergers, and angular momentum transport in neutron stars and accretion disks. Direct simulation of these instabilities are unfeasible, however large-eddy simulations can incorporate the impact of this turbulence with a subgrid model. We present the first machine-learning-based subgrid model for special relativistic magnetohydrodynamics, trained using a neural network. We demonstrate its performance in online simulations of the 3D Kelvin-Helmholtz instability through both a priori and a posteriori tests. Evaluated in a low resolution simulation, our model captures magnetic field amplification of a simulation at 4 times the resolution with a speed-up of a factor 44. This demonstrates the applicability of such methods in general relativistic simulations of neutron star mergers and other scenarios.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a neural network-based subgrid model for magnetic turbulence in special relativistic magnetohydrodynamics that enables efficient and accurate low-resolution simulations, capturing complex magnetic field behavior with significant computational gains.
AI.motivation: Direct simulation of magnetic field instabilities triggering small-scale turbulence in neutron star mergers and related astrophysical contexts is computationally prohibitive, thus necessitating efficient subgrid modeling approaches to accurately capture turbulence effects and associated magnetic field rearrangement.
AI.method: The study introduces a neural network-trained subgrid model for special relativistic magnetohydrodynamics, integrating it into large-eddy simulations to represent unresolved turbulent scales; its performance was validated through both a priori and a posteriori tests in 3D Kelvin-Helmholtz instability simulations.
AI.result: The developed neural network subgrid model accurately reproduced magnetic field amplification from high-resolution simulations in low-resolution runs with a computational speed-up factor of 44, demonstrating its feasibility and effectiveness for application in general relativistic neutron star merger simulations.
AI.conclusion: The machine-learning-based subgrid model effectively captures the impact of small-scale turbulent magnetic field instabilities in low-resolution special relativistic magnetohydrodynamics simulations, enabling realistic magnetic field amplification with significantly enhanced computational efficiency.

title: Revisiting cosmic anisotropy with the Pantheon+ compilation
summary: We investigate cosmic anisotropy within the updated Pantheon+ sample using both the dipole fitting (DF) and hemisphere comparison (HC) methods. With the DF method, the dipole signal within the full sample is statistically weak. However, the low-$z$ subsample yields a dipole signal of $A_{\mathrm{D}} = 0.952^{+0.454}_{-0.403} \times 10^{-3}$ at $\sim 2σ$ significance, pointing towards $(l,b) = (149.77^\circ, -12.20^\circ)$. This signal is predominantly driven by a combined subset of surveys 5, 56, 63, and 150, which is characterized by an amplitude of $A_{\mathrm{D}} = 1.730_{-0.715}^{+0.554} \times 10^{-3}$ towards $(l,b) = (153.05^\circ, -1.25^\circ)$. For the HC method, the full sample yields a maximum anisotropy level of $\mathrm{AL}_{\mathrm{max}} = 0.289 \pm 0.052$ oriented towards $(l,b) = (127.97^\circ, 17.90^\circ)$ with a $1.56σ$ significance. This preferred direction is primarily determined by the highly inhomogeneous SNLS subsample, whereas the low-$z$ and high-$z$ subsamples act to suppress the anisotropy level along this axis. These subsample-dependent results suggest that the apparent anisotropy arises from local structures or the inhomogeneous distribution of the datasets rather than an intrinsic cosmic anisotropy.

AI.tldr: Analyzing the updated Pantheon+ supernova dataset with dipole fitting and hemisphere comparison methods shows weak anisotropy signals driven by data inhomogeneities and local structures, implying no intrinsic cosmic anisotropy.
AI.motivation: To investigate the existence and nature of cosmic anisotropy using updated and comprehensive observational supernova data.
AI.method: Cosmic anisotropy was analyzed using the dipole fitting (DF) and hemisphere comparison (HC) methods applied to the updated Pantheon+ supernovae dataset and its subsamples.
AI.result: The DF method reveals a low-significance dipole signal mainly from combined specific surveys in the low-redshift subsample, while the HC method finds a marginal anisotropy linked to the inhomogeneous SNLS subsample. Overall, the anisotropy signals are attributed to local structures or dataset inhomogeneities rather than cosmic origins.
AI.conclusion: The detected anisotropy signals in the Pantheon+ sample are statistically weak and primarily driven by specific subsamples, suggesting no intrinsic cosmic anisotropy.

title: Getting Tilted: Random Walk of Binary Black Hole Spin-Orbit Alignment in Dense Star Clusters
comment: 25 pages, 8+1 Figures, submitted to ApJ. Comments welcome!
summary: It is commonly assumed that the spin-orbit angles of binary black holes (BBHs) originating from dense stellar environments rapidly converge to an isotropic distribution following a number of strong gravitational encounters. We challenge this assumption by modeling the evolution of the BBH orbital angular momentum orientation through successive binary--single encounters as a random walk on the unit sphere, yielding an exact solution for the orientation distribution after $n$ encounters and a closed-form expression for the number of encounters required to reach isotropy. To characterize the step distribution, we conduct a large suite of Newtonian point-particle scattering experiments with an equal-mass binary, varying the mass of the single, and obtain semi-analytic expressions for both the mean step size and the full distribution of steps. Applying these results to BBHs with initially aligned spins, as may arise from the evolution of primordial massive binaries, we find that spin-orbit alignment can survive several strong encounters before being erased. This has direct implications for the slight trend toward spin-orbit alignment reported in GWTC-5.0 as well as for the retention of hierarchical merger products, such as the components of GW231123.

AI.tldr: This study models BBH spin-orbit angle evolution via random walks, showing that spin alignment can survive multiple encounters in dense stellar environments, challenging the assumption of rapid isotropization and impacting gravitational wave observations.
AI.motivation: To investigate the assumption that spin-orbit angles of binary black holes in dense stellar environments quickly become isotropic after multiple strong gravitational encounters.
AI.method: Modeled the evolution of BBH orbital angular momentum orientation as a random walk on the unit sphere; conducted extensive Newtonian point-particle scattering experiments to characterize the step distribution; derived exact and closed-form expressions for orientation distribution and encounters needed for isotropy.
AI.result: Found that spin-orbit alignment can persist through several strong encounters; the number of encounters needed for isotropy is quantifiable; implications for observed slight spin-orbit alignment trends and hierarchical merger product retention are significant.
AI.conclusion: The assumption of rapid isotropization of BBH spin-orbit angles after strong encounters is challenged, showing spin-orbit alignment can survive multiple encounters, affecting interpretations of gravitational wave data.

title: Fast Radio Burst Cosmology: Hubble Tension and Dark Energy
summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are luminous, millisecond-duration extragalactic radio transients that have emerged as a powerful, complementary cosmological probe for investigating the late-time cosmic evolution, offering unique advantages over conventional probes such as Type Ia supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, and cosmic microwave background radiation. This review systematically summarizes the cosmological applications of FRBs, focusing on their critical roles in measuring the Hubble constant ($H_0$) and constraining dark energy properties. Benefiting from the precise dispersion measure (DM) - redshift relation of localized FRBs, the integrated electron density of the intergalactic medium (IGM) along the line of sight can be tightly modeled, enabling independent and low-redshift measurements of the cosmic expansion rate. Current FRB samples consisting of localized and non-localized events provide competitive $H_0$ constraints, offering an independent method to measure $H_0$. FRBs also serve as effective tracers to constrain dark energy equation-of-state parameters. We comprehensively discuss key limiting factors for FRB cosmological precision, including uncertainties in Galactic and host galaxy electron density models, and IGM inhomogeneities. With the rapid growth of high-precision FRB surveys and localized FRB samples, FRBs are promising to provide stringent constraints on late-time cosmic acceleration, dark energy evolution and cosmic baryons.

AI.tldr: This review highlights the emerging role of fast radio bursts as precise cosmological tools for measuring the Hubble constant and dark energy properties, overcoming limitations of traditional probes via their dispersion measure-redshift relations, with promising future prospects despite current modeling uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To explore and summarize the utility of fast radio bursts (FRBs) as a novel cosmological probe for late-time cosmic evolution, given their unique advantages over traditional methods.
AI.method: Systematic review and analysis of the cosmological applications of FRBs, focusing on their dispersion measure (DM) - redshift relations, modeling of intergalactic medium electron density, and the use of localized and non-localized FRB samples to measure cosmic parameters.
AI.result: Current FRB data yield competitive independent constraints on the Hubble constant ($H_0$) and dark energy equation-of-state parameters. Despite challenges posed by uncertainties in electron density models and intergalactic medium inhomogeneities, FRBs show promise for precise cosmological measurements in the near future.
AI.conclusion: FRBs constitute a powerful complementary cosmological probe capable of providing independent measurements of cosmic expansion and stringent constraints on dark energy and cosmic baryons, with their utility set to increase as high-precision surveys and localized samples grow.

title: A grid of fast-rotating, chemically-homogeneous, supernova and/or long-GRB progenitors
comment: submitted to AAS, data available at https://zenodo.org/records/14286306, reproducible at https://github.com/mathren/CHE_LGRB_progenitors, comments welcome!
summary: The understanding of the mechanism(s) by which massive stars collapse and possibly explode is rapidly maturing. Uncertainties in the structure of the stellar core at the onset of collapse are often dominant in numerical simulations, and a limited number of progenitor grids are available. This is especially true for explosions where rotation and magnetic fields play a significant or primary role. We present a grid of 113 single-star models with initial masses $M_{\rm ZAMS}=30-90\,M_{\odot}$ and initial rigid rotation $ω_{\rm ZAMS}=0.5-0.99\,ω_{\rm crit}$ computed at $Z=0.001$ with the open-source stellar evolution code \textsc{MESA}. We adopt a 128-isotope nuclear reaction network capable of following the weak reactions deleptonizing the core during and after silicon core burning. By construction, these models experience rotationally-induced chemically-homogeneous evolution, and reach the onset of collapse ($v_{\rm infall}\lesssim -300\,\mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$) with large and structured amounts of angular momentum, possibly sufficient to form accretion disks on a proto-compact object. Therefore, these progenitor structures provide a homogeneous set of models with updated input physics and improved algorithmic accuracy to understand stellar explosions of (some types of) stripped-envelope supernovae, possibly jetted and/or broad-lined, collapsars or magnetar-powered, and/or long $γ$-ray bursts.

AI.tldr: This study presents 113 rapidly rotating massive star models evolved with detailed nuclear networks, offering a homogeneous and updated dataset to investigate rotation-influenced core-collapse explosions and corresponding transient events such as certain supernovae and gamma-ray bursts.
AI.motivation: To improve understanding of the collapse and explosion mechanisms of massive stars, focusing on the influence of rotation and magnetic fields on stellar core structure at collapse onset.
AI.method: Computed a grid of 113 single-star models with initial masses 30–90 solar masses and initial rigid rotation 0.5–0.99 of critical rotation, at metallicity Z=0.001, using the MESA code with a 128-isotope nuclear reaction network including weak reactions during silicon burning, simulating chemically homogeneous evolution up to collapse with high angular momentum.
AI.result: Generated a homogeneous set of progenitor models exhibiting large, structured angular momentum distributions capable of forming accretion disks around proto-compact objects, suitable for studying various explosion scenarios like jetted/broad-lined supernovae, collapsars, magnetar-powered events, and long gamma-ray bursts.
AI.conclusion: The presented model grid provides an improved and consistent dataset of rapidly rotating massive star progenitors at low metallicity, enhancing the understanding of rotation-driven explosion mechanisms and related transient phenomena.

title: Shape-Preserving Evolution of the Global Ultraviolet Quasar Luminosity Function to $z\simeq7.5$
summary: We present a global unbinned-likelihood analysis of the rest-frame ultraviolet (UV) quasar luminosity function (QLF) over $0.1\le z\le7.5$, using a final analysis sample of 70,960 Type~1 quasars selected from the homogenized compilation of Kulkarni et al. (2019). We test a shape-preserving luminosity and density evolution (LADE) framework, in which the local luminosity function (LF) shape is fixed and the redshift evolution is described by separate density- and luminosity-evolution factors. For a double-power-law (DPL) local LF, we search 81 LADE models built from nine density-evolution and nine luminosity-evolution functions, and compare them with two flexible double-power-law (FDPL) reference models. The fiducial shape-preserving LADE model gives the lowest Akaike information criterion (AIC) and Bayesian information criterion (BIC) values among the main models considered, and 12 DPL-based LADE models have lower AIC and BIC values than both FDPL reference models. Repeating the model-grid analysis with a modified-Schechter local LF gives the same preferred evolutionary structure, indicating that the result is not driven only by the assumed local LF shape. The fitted evolution functions further show that the luminosity-evolution component is the more stable part of the LADE decomposition: it rises rapidly to $z\simeq2$--3 and then flattens or slowly declines. The density-evolution component is more model dependent, but the preferred LADE models consistently require a declining effective normalization toward high redshift. Taken together, we conclude that a shape-preserving framework offers a statistically efficient and compact empirical description of the global UV QLF.

AI.tldr: The study uses a large quasar sample to test shape-preserving luminosity and density evolution models of the UV quasar luminosity function over a wide redshift range. The LADE models, especially the fiducial one, outperform flexible reference models, offering a statistically efficient and consistent description of quasar luminosity and density evolution with redshift.
AI.motivation: To achieve a statistically efficient and compact empirical description of the global rest-frame ultraviolet quasar luminosity function (QLF) spanning a wide redshift range (0.1 to 7.5).
AI.method: A global unbinned-likelihood analysis was performed using a homogenized sample of 70,960 Type 1 quasars. The analysis tested a shape-preserving luminosity and density evolution (LADE) framework by exploring 81 models constructed from combinations of nine density-evolution and nine luminosity-evolution functions based on a double-power-law local luminosity function (LF).
