Results were compared to two flexible double-power-law (FDPL) reference models, and robustness was checked using a modified-Schechter local LF.
AI.result: The fiducial shape-preserving LADE model yielded the lowest Akaike information criterion (AIC) and Bayesian information criterion (BIC) values, outperforming FDPL models. Twelve other DPL-based LADE models also showed lower AIC and BIC scores than FDPL models. The preferred evolutionary structure was consistent regardless of the local LF shape, with a luminosity-evolution component rising sharply to redshift ~2–3 then flattening or declining, and a density-evolution component requiring a declining normalization at high redshift. These findings support the LADE framework as an effective empirical approach to model the global UV QLF.
AI.conclusion: The shape-preserving LADE framework provides a statistically robust, compact, and stable empirical description of the global UV quasar luminosity function across a broad redshift range, outperforming more flexible models in model selection criteria and offering insight into the distinct evolutionary behaviors of luminosity and density components.

title: Do Prompt Gamma-ray Burst Fireball Composition Impact on Afterglow Emission? Cases Study for Long GRBs 080916C/090902B and Short GRBs 090510/130603B
comment: 13 pages, 4 figures, 1 table, Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Broadband observations with the {\em Fermi} mission reveal that a large fraction of gamma-ray burst (GRB) spectra are dominated by non-thermal emission, while a small fraction are dominated by thermal/quasi-thermal emission, likely indicating the difference in jet composition among GRB. By selecting two typical long GRBs (080916C and 090902B) and two short GRBs (130603B and 090510), we present a comparative analysis to investigate whether the composition of prompt GRB jets influences the afterglow emission for bursts originating from both massive star collapse and compact binary mergers. Incorporating emission from both primary and cascade electron populations, we fit the multi-wavelength afterglow lightcurves of these GRBs with the standard forward shock model and analyze the particle acceleration and radiation physics of the jets. Our results show that the afterglow lightcurve evolution with the characteristic parameters is not related to the composition of the GRB fireball but rather depends on the ambient medium density. The early UV-optical afterglows of the two long GRBs are dominated by synchrotron emission from cascaded $e^{\pm}$ pairs produced via the $γγ$ annihilation process, whereas this is not the case for the two short GRBs. These results suggest that the internal energy of the fireball is converted into jet kinetic energy during the prompt phase, and that the fireball composition leaves no detectable footprint on the afterglow jet. Instead, the density of the ambient medium plays an essential role in shaping the afterglow emission.

AI.tldr: This study shows that GRB afterglow emissions are influenced mainly by the ambient medium density, not the jet composition; early afterglows in long GRBs involve cascaded pairs synchrotron emission, whereas short GRBs do not exhibit this feature.
AI.motivation: Investigate whether the composition of prompt gamma-ray burst (GRB) jets affects the afterglow emission for bursts from both massive star collapse and compact binary mergers.
AI.method: Select two typical long GRBs and two short GRBs; fit their multi-wavelength afterglow lightcurves using the standard forward shock model incorporating emission from primary and cascade electron populations; analyze particle acceleration and radiation physics of the jets.
AI.result: Afterglow lightcurve evolution depends on ambient medium density rather than GRB fireball composition; early UV-optical afterglows in long GRBs are dominated by synchrotron emission from cascaded electron-positron pairs, unlike in short GRBs; fireball composition leaves no detectable footprint on the afterglow jet.
AI.conclusion: The internal energy of the fireball converts into jet kinetic energy during the prompt phase, and the ambient medium density, not fireball composition, primarily shapes the afterglow emission.

title: Tracing Large-scale Structure with the MeerKLASS On-the-Fly Survey: Angular Clustering of Radio Sources at 816 MHz
summary: We present the first measurement of the angular two-point correlation function \(w(θ)\) of radio sources from the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) UHF on-the-fly (OTF) continuum Data Release~1. DR1 provides interferometric Stokes-\(I\) imaging at a reference frequency of 816\,MHz over \(\sim 800~\mathrm{deg}^2\) within the DESI footprint. We detect a positive clustering signal over \(0.02^\circ \lesssim θ\lesssim 10^\circ\). The measurement is stable to reasonable variations of the depth mask and flux threshold on intermediate and large scales. Modelling the intermediate-scale signal (\(0.112^\circ\leθ\le 1.36^\circ\)) with a fixed-slope power law (\(γ=1.8\)) yields \(A(1^\circ)=(1.434\pm0.475)\times10^{-3}\), corresponding to \(\log_{10}A=-2.843^{+0.124}_{-0.175}\). We infer an effective large-scale bias by fitting \(Λ\)CDM projected-matter templates \(w_{\rm DM}(θ)\) computed with \textsc{CAMB} and Limber projection, including an integral-constraint correction evaluated from random--random weights. Using two bracketing T-RECS redshift-distribution priors, we obtain \(b_{\rm eff}=1.998\pm0.350\) (AGN prior) and \(b_{\rm eff}=1.530\pm0.265\) (TOTAL prior), demonstrating that the dominant modelling uncertainty arises from \(N(z)\). As a derived summary we Limber-invert the power-law amplitude to obtain \(r_0=6.18\pm1.13\) and \(5.59\pm1.02~h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}\) for the AGN and TOTAL priors, respectively. These results establish MeerKLASS UHF DR1 as a new wide-area, intermediate-frequency dataset for radio-continuum clustering. As MeerKLASS expands and overlapping optical/IR spectroscopy provides improved redshift calibration, future releases will enable population-split clustering and bias evolution measurements with substantially reduced modelling uncertainty.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first measurement of radio source angular clustering from MeerKLASS UHF DR1, detecting significant clustering and deriving effective bias values, establishing the dataset's utility for future cosmological and astrophysical studies with improved redshift information.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to measure the angular two-point correlation function of radio sources in the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey to understand the clustering properties of radio sources at intermediate frequencies over a large sky area.
AI.method: The study analyses interferometric Stokes-I imaging data at 816 MHz over approximately 800 deg², models the angular correlation function on intermediate angular scales using a fixed-slope power law, fits ΛCDM matter templates computed via CAMB and Limber projection to infer large-scale bias, and examines the impact of redshift distribution priors from T-RECS.
AI.result: A positive clustering signal is detected over angular scales from 0.02° to 10°, with a modeled power-law amplitude A(1°) = (1.434±0.475)×10^{-3} and effective bias values of 1.998±0.350 (AGN prior) and 1.530±0.265 (TOTAL prior). The correlation length r_0 is derived as ∼6.18±1.13 and ∼5.59±1.02 h^{-1} Mpc respectively, highlighting significant uncertainty from redshift distribution modeling.
AI.conclusion: MeerKLASS UHF DR1 constitutes a robust, wide-area intermediate-frequency radio-continuum clustering dataset. Future data releases with improved redshift calibrations and population segregation will reduce modeling uncertainties and enable detailed studies of clustering and bias evolution in radio source populations.

title: Intraday Optical Variability of BL Lacertae during its Highly Active 2020-2024 Phase
summary: We present an analysis of the intraday flux and spectral variability of BL Lacertae from 2020 September 30 to 2024 December 7, covering its highest recorded brightness and low, intermediate, and high flux states. Our study involved 62 nights of multi-band (BVRI) optical monitoring using four ground-based telescopes located in Egypt, Türkiye, and Bulgaria. We assessed intraday flux variability using the power-enhanced F-test and the nested ANOVA test. Significant variability was detected in 88 out of 117 light curves, consistent with previous studies of this object during active epochs. The maximum variability amplitude is 44.5 per cent in the B band. Spectral analysis reveals a bluer-when-brighter trend during intraday flares, supporting a synchrotron origin for the variable emission. For a subset of well-sampled flares, we model their profiles with a double exponential function, deriving rise and decay time-scales, thereby constraining the characteristic times of particle acceleration and cooling processes within the relativistic jet. Assuming a turbulent jet model, we determined limits on the radii and magnetic field strengths of the emitting regions. We detected soft time lags for a multi-band flare and from their analysis, derived the Doppler factor and magnetic field strength of the corresponding emitting region. Our long-term, high-cadence study confirms that BL Lacertae was in an exceptionally active phase during the 2020-2024 period, with intraday variability being a common phenomenon. The results underscore the dynamic nature of the jet emission region and provide valuable observational constraints for models of blazar variability and jet physics.

AI.tldr: The study analyzed multi-band optical data of BL Lacertae from 2020 to 2024, revealing frequent significant intraday variability and a bluer-when-brighter trend. Modeling flare profiles and timing yielded insights on particle acceleration, cooling processes, and physical conditions in the jet, confirming an exceptionally active phase and informing blazar jet models.
AI.motivation: To understand the intraday flux and spectral variability of BL Lacertae across different flux states including its highest recorded brightness, providing insights into the dynamic processes in the relativistic jet.
AI.method: Multi-band (BVRI) optical monitoring over 62 nights using four ground-based telescopes, with intraday variability assessed via power-enhanced F-test and nested ANOVA; spectral analysis and flare profile modeling with double exponential functions; application of turbulent jet model to derive physical parameters.
AI.result: Detected significant intraday variability in 88 of 117 light curves, with maximum amplitude of 44.5% in B band; confirmed bluer-when-brighter trend supporting synchrotron emission; constrained particle acceleration and cooling timescales; derived emitting region radii, magnetic field strengths, Doppler factor from variability and time lag analysis; established BL Lacertae's highly active phase from 2020-2024.
AI.conclusion: BL Lacertae exhibits frequent and significant intraday variability driven by dynamic jet processes. The findings confirm a synchrotron origin of variability and provide important constraints on the physical conditions of the emitting region, enhancing models of blazar variability and relativistic jet physics.

title: Radio spectral properties and aging of two tailed radio galaxies in a galaxy group at z=0.35
summary: We present a study of two tailed radio galaxies in the core of a massive, dynamically young galaxy group - an early group-group merger. Using VLA (3 GHz and 1.4 GHz), MeerKAT (1.35 GHz), and GMRT (610 and 325 MHz) observations, we investigate their radio spectral properties, spectral and dynamical ages. Radio morphologies show clear evidence of interaction with the intragroup medium (IGM). One galaxy is a wide-angle tail (WAT) source, while the other is most likely a head-tail (HT) galaxy. Both galaxies exhibit high radio luminosities, and we find spectral indices of $α=0.8\pm 0.1$ (WAT) and $α=0.6\pm 0.2$ (HT). Spectral index analysis reveals spectral steepening with distance from the core in both galaxies, with localized flattening in the WAT lobes and hotspots along the northern jet, and indications of such flattening in the middle of the HT tail. Spectral ages derived using Jaffe-Perola model are $33.80\substack{+7.63 \\ -7.23}$ Myr (WAT) and $20.86\substack{+10.07 \\ -17.17}$ Myr (HT), significantly lower than dynamical ages of $420\pm60$ to $700\pm100$ Myr (WAT) and $140\pm20$ Myr (and possibly up to $280\pm40$ Myr, for HT), yielding dynamical-to-spectral age ratios of $\sim12-20$ and $\sim7$ (and up to $\sim14$), respectively. The discrepancy may be reduced by using more complex dynamical age models, incorporating interactions with the IGM, which requires deeper X-ray observations of the group. Spectral age estimates may be affected by mixing of electron populations, and could be better constrained with future deep, high-resolution broad-band radio observations at both MHz and frequencies above 3 GHz. The combination of extended radio structures, spectral signatures of radiative aging with localized re-acceleration, and activity timescales up to hundreds of Myr indicates that galaxies are actively interacting with, and likely depositing energy into their environment.

AI.tldr: A multi-frequency radio study of two tailed radio galaxies in a young galaxy group reveals active interaction with the environment, age discrepancies between spectral and dynamical estimates, and evidence of ongoing particle re-acceleration and energy input into the intragroup medium.
AI.motivation: To investigate the radio spectral properties, spectral and dynamical ages, and interactions of two tailed radio galaxies in a dynamically young galaxy group undergoing an early group-group merger.
AI.method: Multi-frequency radio observations were conducted using VLA (3 GHz and 1.4 GHz), MeerKAT (1.35 GHz), and GMRT (610 and 325 MHz) to analyze radio morphologies, spectral indices, and spectral ages using the Jaffe-Perola model; dynamical ages were also estimated and compared.
AI.result: The study found the galaxies to be a wide-angle tail (WAT) and a head-tail (HT) source with high radio luminosities and spectral steepening away from the cores. Spectral ages (∼20-34 Myr) were significantly lower than dynamical ages (∼140-700 Myr), with age ratios of approximately 7-20, suggesting the need for more complex models considering IGM interactions. Evidence of localized re-acceleration and energy deposition into the environment was observed.
AI.conclusion: The two tailed radio galaxies are actively interacting with their intragroup medium, exhibiting radiative aging and localized particle re-acceleration over timescales of up to hundreds of Myr, implying ongoing energy deposition and environmental impact. More detailed observations are needed to reconcile age discrepancies and refine models of their dynamical evolution.

title: Fast Optical Variability of the TeV Blazar PKS 1725+123 Observed by SVOM-VT and Insights from Multi-wavelength Follow-up Observations
comment: 23 pages, 8 figures, accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: PKS 1725+123 is a flat-spectrum radio quasar (FSRQ) with a redshift of $z=0.586$. The detection of this object in the TeV band was reported by the MAGIC telescopes and H.E.S.S. in August 2025. Subsequently, we promptly initiated Target-of-Opportunity observations using the Space-based multi-band astronomical Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) satellite. By analyzing the observational optical data from SVOM-VT and comprehensively examining the Fermi-LAT and Swift-XRT observational data, it was found that the source is in a high-flux state across the optical, X-ray, and GeV $γ$-ray bands around the time of the TeV detections. Its optical flux reaches a historically unprecedented high level and shows significant variability on timescale as short as minutes. The variability is accompanied by changes in the color index, exhibiting a \textit{bluer when brighter} behavior during the high-flux state. Based on the simultaneous multi-wavelength data, we construct the broadband spectral energy distribution (SED) of the source in the high-flux state. PKS 1725+123 demonstrates a remarkably high synchrotron peak frequency, which is distinctly different from that of other FSRQs. We propose a two-zone spine-sheath jet model to reproduce this SED. The optical--X-ray emission is generated by the synchrotron process of the relativistic electrons within a compact zone. The inverse Compton (IC) scattering processes of the same electron population contribute to the low-energy end of the Fermi-LAT spectrum, while the high-energy end of the Fermi-LAT spectrum is ascribed to the IC scattering of the synchrotron photons within the compact zone by the higher-energy electrons in an extended region.

AI.tldr: PKS 1725+123, detected in TeV gamma rays, exhibited record high flux and rapid variability across optical to GeV bands. A two-zone jet model involving synchrotron and inverse Compton processes explains its unusual spectral energy distribution.
AI.motivation: The study is motivated by the recent detection of the FSRQ PKS 1725+123 in the TeV band and the need to understand its multi-wavelength high-flux state and unusual spectral properties.
AI.method: The researchers conducted Target-of-Opportunity observations with the SVOM satellite and analyzed its optical data, along with archival Fermi-LAT and Swift-XRT data, to monitor flux states and variability. They constructed broadband SEDs and applied a two-zone spine-sheath jet model to interpret the emission mechanisms.
AI.result: PKS 1725+123 was found to be in an unprecedented high-flux state across optical, X-ray, and GeV gamma-ray bands, with rapid variability and 'bluer when brighter' color behavior. The source exhibits a high synchrotron peak frequency unique among FSRQs. The two-zone model successfully reproduces the broadband SED with synchrotron emission from a compact zone and inverse Compton scattering contributing to gamma rays in different jet regions.
AI.conclusion: The multi-wavelength observations reveal that PKS 1725+123 shows extraordinary flux levels and spectral characteristics not typical for FSRQs. The two-zone spine-sheath jet model explains the observed emission features and clarifies the origin of the broadband high-flux emission.

title: Understanding the non-Gaussian nature of Galactic foreground emissions towards small scales
summary: We present a unified, multi-scale study of non-Gaussianity of Galactic foreground emissions using Minkowski Functionals and generalized skewness-kurtosis parameters, focusing on the characterization of small-scale non-Gaussianity and its underlying physical origin. We find that all foreground components studied exhibit a remarkably universal non-Gaussian nature dominated by excess kurtosis, whose shape remains stable across angular scales despite large differences in emission physics. Focusing on thermal dust, we perform a detailed comparison between observed maps (GNILC and Planck 545 GHz) and dust model realizations (PySM and filament-based models) to assess the performance of state-of-the-art models in reproducing the observed non-Gaussian properties. At the global level, GNILC and PySM display closely matched kurtosis behavior over the angular scales where the GNILC reconstruction is reliable, while the filament-based model produces substantially weaker skewness and kurtosis signals. For PySM, however, a patch-based analysis reveals statistically significant regional variations, indicating that while the model reproduces the overall non-Gaussian amplitude and scale dependence, it does not fully capture the spatial variability of the observed kurtosis signal. Using simple PDF-based toy models, we demonstrate that the universal kurtosis signature arises from the combination of heavy-tailed one-point statistics and steep large-scale spatial correlations, while its detailed amplitude and scale dependence depend on the underlying foreground physics. These results identify excess kurtosis as a robust statistical fingerprint of Galactic foregrounds and provide a practical framework for validating small-scale foreground models for future CMB analyses.

AI.tldr: This study identifies excess kurtosis as a universal and robust signature of Galactic foreground non-Gaussianity, validates current dust models against observations, and offers a practical approach to improve foreground modeling for accurate CMB analysis.
AI.motivation: To characterize the small-scale non-Gaussianity of Galactic foreground emissions and understand its physical origin, improving modeling for future Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) analyses.
AI.method: A unified, multi-scale analysis using Minkowski Functionals and generalized skewness-kurtosis parameters applied to observed foreground maps (GNILC, Planck 545 GHz) and dust models (PySM, filament-based), including both global and patch-based comparisons and toy PDF-based models.
AI.result: All foreground components show a universal non-Gaussianity dominated by excess kurtosis stable across angular scales; GNILC and PySM models match observed kurtosis globally but PySM shows regional variability; filament-based models underpredict skewness and kurtosis; excess kurtosis arises from heavy-tailed one-point statistics combined with steep large-scale spatial correlations.
AI.conclusion: Excess kurtosis serves as a robust statistical fingerprint for Galactic foregrounds and provides a useful framework for validating and improving small-scale foreground models essential for precision CMB studies.

title: Multiwavelength variability of the high-energy neutrino candidate PKS 0735+178 over three decades
summary: We present the multiwavelength variability of the BL Lac object PKS 0735+178, associated with the high-energy neutrino event IC211208A. The light curves cover the radio (1-230 GHz), optical, and Fermi-LAT $γ$-ray bands over a $\sim$30 years time-scale. The light curves are correlated, with delays from 0 to 1200 days increasing towards lower frequencies, consistent with emission from an opacity-stratified jet. The bright flare after the IC211208A event indicates emission from a compact, optically thick region with enhanced activity and more efficient particle acceleration. Short optical and $γ$-ray bursts have been detected very close to the neutrino event, within a few days. The $\sim$12-day lag between the $γ$-ray and optical emissions is detected for the first time, suggesting that the emission regions are not co-spatial. A characteristic variability time-scale of $\sim$10-11 yr is robustly detected in the radio-mm bands ($\geq3σ$), while the optical and $γ$-ray data show weaker, shorter-period signals. The independent constraints from the VLBI core-shift measurements and radio time delays yield consistent estimates of the jet geometry and disturbance propagation, supporting variability governed by jet propagation effects. The long-term modulation is consistent with a slow variation in energy release at the jet base, while individual flares arise from shocks propagating downstream. Jet precession may contribute to the long-term modulation; however, the required viewing angles are inconsistent with the VLBI constraints, indicating that precession alone cannot explain the observed variability.

AI.tldr: Thirty years of multiwavelength monitoring of BL Lac object PKS 0735+178 reveal correlated variability with frequency-dependent delays and a newly found ~12-day γ-ray to optical lag. Long-term radio-mm variability aligns with jet propagation effects, supporting a model of slow energy release changes at the jet base and shock-induced flares, while rejecting jet precession as the sole variability cause.
AI.motivation: To investigate the multiwavelength variability of the BL Lac object PKS 0735+178 and its association with the high-energy neutrino event IC211208A, aiming to understand the emission mechanisms and jet dynamics over long timescales.
AI.method: Analysis of multi-frequency light curves spanning radio (1-230 GHz), optical, and Fermi-LAT γ-ray bands covering ~30 years, including correlation and time-lag studies, VLBI core-shift measurements, and modeling jet geometry and propagation effects.
AI.result: Detection of correlated variability across bands with frequency-dependent time delays indicating opacity-stratified jet emission; identification of a ~12-day lag between γ-ray and optical emissions; robust long-term (~10-11 year) variability in radio-mm bands; consistent jet geometry and propagation parameters from independent measurements; and rejection of jet precession as sole cause of variability.
AI.conclusion: The variability of PKS 0735+178 is governed by jet propagation effects with slow variations at the jet base modulating long-term variability, while individual flares correspond to shocks downstream. Jet precession alone cannot explain observed patterns due to inconsistent viewing angle constraints.

title: A cross-calibration approach for polarisation-sensitive detectors in CMB experiments: application to LiteBIRD's polarisation angle calibration
summary: One of the current challenges in observational cosmology is obtaining high-precision polarisation maps of the CMB to measure primordial $B$-modes and constrain the tensor-to-scalar ratio ($r$). The weakness of this signal compared to foregrounds and $E$-to-$B$ leakage makes this task particularly challenging, requiring large detector arrays operating at multiple frequencies and extremely precise calibration. We present a cross-calibration algorithm to determine relative calibration of detectors within the same frequency band of a CMB experiment. The method iteratively compares single-detector maps with band-averaged maps and can be applied to any calibration parameter that can be observed and corrected at the map level, relaxing pre-flight calibration requirements and enabling post-processing validation. We validate the pipeline by calibrating the polarisation angle of simulated LiteBIRD observations, including both random detector miscalibration and wafer-level rotations. The algorithm converges to correct values with arcminute precision. Finally, we propagate residual calibration uncertainties through component separation and tensor-to-scalar ratio estimation pipelines using both parametric (FgBuster) and blind (HILC) methods. The induced bias on $r$ remains well below the LiteBIRD systematics budget of $δr < 6.5\times10^{-6}$, demonstrating that the method is suitable for next-generation CMB experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a cross-calibration algorithm for precise detector calibration in CMB polarization experiments, validated on simulated LiteBIRD data, achieving high accuracy and ensuring minimal bias on the tensor-to-scalar ratio measurement.
AI.motivation: Measuring primordial B-modes in the CMB to constrain the tensor-to-scalar ratio is challenged by weak signals, foregrounds, and E-to-B leakage requiring precise calibration.
AI.method: A cross-calibration algorithm iteratively compares single-detector maps to band-averaged maps within the same frequency band to determine relative calibration parameters at the map level.
AI.result: The algorithm accurately calibrates detector polarisation angles with arcminute precision in simulated LiteBIRD data and residual calibration uncertainties induce a bias on the tensor-to-scalar ratio well below the systematic budget.
AI.conclusion: The proposed cross-calibration method effectively enables precise in-band relative calibration post-launch, relaxing pre-flight requirements and supporting robust tensor-to-scalar ratio estimation for future CMB experiments.

title: Crust glass formation reveals the neutron star birth properties in IGR J17480-2446
comment: 12 pages, 2 figures, accepted in Phys. Rev. Letters
summary: IGR J17480-2446 is a low-mass X-ray binary, harboring an exceptional accreting pulsar (a neutron star) with an unusual spin frequency of 11 Hz and a very slow post-outburst crust cooling. The former may imply that it is observed at an early stage of recycling, while the latter was shown to indicate the presence in the outer crust of a low thermal conductivity layer, possibly made of glass. Here we argue that the glass layer formation is a natural result of accretion induced failure of pristine cold crystal crust. This allows us to determine the mass of the accreted material as $ΔM \approx 2.4\times 10^{-6}~M_\odot$, confirming very early accretion stage for this neutron star. An analysis of spin and thermal state reveals a peculiar set of neutron star birth properties which is commonly associated with `recycled' neutron stars, i.e.\ those that have been experiencing prolonged periods of accretion from a companion. We speculate that such birth properties may represent the outcome of neutron star formation in an electron-capture supernova.

AI.tldr: IGR J17480-2446 is an early-stage recycled neutron star exhibiting slow crust cooling due to a glassy low-conductivity crust layer formed by accretion-induced crust failure, with properties hinting at an electron-capture supernova origin.
AI.motivation: To understand the unusual spin frequency and slow post-outburst crust cooling of the neutron star in IGR J17480-2446, and to explore the implications for its accretion history and crust composition.
AI.method: The study analyzes the cooling behavior and spin properties of the neutron star, linking the crust cooling to the formation of a low thermal conductivity glass layer caused by accretion-induced failure of the original crust. It quantitatively estimates the accreted mass and examines birth properties based on thermal and spin data.
AI.result: The formation of a glassy crust layer is naturally explained by accretion-induced crust failure, allowing determination of a small accreted mass (~2.4×10⁻⁶ solar masses), confirming the neutron star is in a very early recycling stage. The neutron star’s birth properties align with those typical of recycled neutron stars, possibly originating from electron-capture supernovae.
AI.conclusion: The unusual spin frequency and slow cooling of IGR J17480-2446 are consequences of early-stage recycling and crustal changes induced by accretion. This supports the idea that the neutron star's birth resulted from an electron-capture supernova and that the crust contains a glass layer formed during accretion.

title: Wedge-avoidance Fisher Forecasts for Primordial Non-Gaussianity from Dark-Ages 21-cm Power Spectrum and Bispectrum
summary: The Dark Ages offer a uniquely clean window on primordial physics, making the redshifted 21-cm signal a promising probe of primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG). Forecasts for interferometric 21-cm measurements must account for foreground wedge avoidance, which removes a substantial fraction of Fourier modes, and this effect is especially severe at high redshifts. We develop a wedge-aware Fisher framework in which this mode loss is propagated directly into the variances of the cylindrical 21-cm power spectrum and reduced bispectrum. As a case study, we apply the method to forecast PNG constraints in two inflation models with different oscillatory features, a resonant model and a step model, for a lunar far-side array including thermal noise. Since these features affect both the power spectrum and the bispectrum, we apply wedge avoidance to both forecasts and compare their constraining power on PNG amplitudes in these oscillatory feature models. We find that wedge avoidance reduces available Fourier modes significantly in both observables, leading to much weaker constraints on PNG. This framework is broadly applicable to 21-cm power spectrum and bispectrum forecasts across redshifts and is particularly useful in regimes where foreground wedge effect is severe, such as the epoch of reionization and the higher-redshift Dark Ages.

AI.tldr: This work introduces a Fisher matrix method that accounts for foreground wedge mode loss in 21-cm power spectrum and bispectrum forecasts, demonstrating that wedge avoidance critically weakens constraints on primordial non-Gaussianity, especially during the Dark Ages and reionization epoch, using lunar far-side array scenarios.
AI.motivation: To enable accurate forecasts of primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) constraints from 21-cm interferometric measurements at high redshifts, accounting for the severe data loss due to foreground wedge avoidance.
AI.method: Developed a wedge-aware Fisher matrix framework that incorporates the mode loss from foreground wedge avoidance directly into the variances of the cylindrical 21-cm power spectrum and reduced bispectrum, applied to two inflation models with oscillatory features, using a lunar far-side array including thermal noise considerations.
AI.result: Wedge avoidance significantly reduces the number of usable Fourier modes in both the power spectrum and bispectrum observables, leading to substantially weaker constraints on PNG amplitudes. The framework is broadly applicable across redshifts where wedge effects are severe.
AI.conclusion: Foreground wedge avoidance poses a critical challenge to constraining primordial non-Gaussianity with 21-cm observations by substantially reducing available Fourier modes, but the developed wedge-aware Fisher framework provides a robust method for propagating these effects into forecasts, improving reliability of PNG constraints in the Dark Ages and epoch of reionization regimes.

title: Fast targeted gravitational-wave followup search for compact binary mergers using GSTLAL pipeline
summary: We present a novel method to conduct targeted gravitational-wave searches for compact binary mergers using the GstLAL inspiral pipeline. By incorporating sky localization and timing information from external electromagnetic triggers, we enhance the sensitivity of the search for sub-threshold gravitational-wave signals associated with events such as short gamma-ray bursts. Our approach modifies the standard likelihood ratio ranking statistic to include a sky localization prior, allowing for a more focused analysis on specific regions of the sky. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through injection studies, comparing the performance of the targeted search against the standard all-sky search configuration. The results show a significant improvement in detection efficiency for signals consistent with the provided sky location and timing, while maintaining control over false alarm rates. This targeted search framework enables rapid follow-up of electromagnetic transients, facilitating multi-messenger astronomy efforts in the era of advanced gravitational-wave detectors.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a targeted gravitational-wave search method using the GstLAL pipeline that integrates electromagnetic trigger data to improve detection of compact binary mergers, enhancing multi-messenger astronomy capabilities.
AI.motivation: Improve the detection sensitivity of gravitational-wave signals associated with electromagnetic events such as short gamma-ray bursts by leveraging external sky localization and timing data.
AI.method: Modify the GstLAL inspiral pipeline's likelihood ratio ranking statistic to incorporate a sky localization prior, enabling targeted searches focused on specific sky regions indicated by electromagnetic triggers.
AI.result: Injection studies show significant improvement in detection efficiency for signals matching the sky location and timing, with controlled false alarm rates compared to the standard all-sky search.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating sky localization and timing information from electromagnetic triggers in gravitational-wave searches enhances sensitivity and enables rapid, focused multi-messenger follow-up using the GstLAL pipeline.

title: Field-level weak lensing cosmology with $<100$ simulations using multifidelity simulation-based inference
summary: We perform a realistic KiDS-Legacy mock analysis with field-level neural compression and simulation-based inference using fewer than 100 $N$-body simulations. The weak lensing shear field encodes substantially more cosmological information than standard two-point summary statistics such as the power spectrum. Field-level inference can fully exploit this information, but physical realism at the field-level requires very high-fidelity simulations. This poses a major challenge for simulation-based inference (SBI): accurate empirical density modelling and deep-learning-based neural compression require many training simulations, but achieving physical realism at the field level makes each simulation extremely costly. We demonstrate that multifidelity SBI can alleviate this tension by substantially reducing the number of high-fidelity simulations needed for accurate cosmological inference. We pre-train neural inference models on realistic KiDS-Legacy-like shear mocks using fast log-normal GLASS simulations and fine-tune them on a small set of high-fidelity $N$-body simulations. We show that between $60$-$100$ high-fidelity simulations are sufficient to obtain informative and well-calibrated cosmological posteriors, enabling an order-of-magnitude reduction in simulation cost for accurate field-level inference in a realistic setting.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that by combining fast approximate simulations with a limited number of high-fidelity N-body simulations via multifidelity SBI and neural compression, one can efficiently and accurately extract cosmological information from weak lensing shear fields, reducing computational costs significantly.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of obtaining accurate cosmological inferences from weak lensing shear fields, which encode more information than standard summaries but require costly high-fidelity simulations for field-level realism.
AI.method: They use multifidelity simulation-based inference by pre-training neural inference models on fast, approximate GLASS simulations followed by fine-tuning on a small number (60-100) of high-fidelity N-body simulations to achieve efficient and accurate field-level inference.
AI.result: They achieve informative and well-calibrated cosmological posteriors using fewer than 100 high-fidelity simulations, reducing computation costs by an order of magnitude while maintaining physical realism and accuracy in a realistic KiDS-Legacy mock analysis.
AI.conclusion: Multifidelity simulation-based inference leveraging neural compression allows accurate and computationally efficient cosmological parameter inference at the field level from weak lensing data, enabling substantial reduction in the number of expensive simulations required.

title: EMU discovery of Thunder: a bow-shock PWN powered by PSR J1631-4722 escaping Nimbus SNR (G336.7+0.5)
comment: 12 figures, 8 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We report the discovery of a bow-shock pulsar wind nebula (PWN), dubbed Thunder, powered by the radio pulsar PSR J1631-4722 and projected within the Galactic supernova remnant (SNR) G336.7+0.5 (Nimbus). The system was first identified in observations from the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey and further characterised using MeerKAT Galactic Plane Survey data together with follow-up observations at 5.5 and 9 GHz obtained with the Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA). Assuming a distance of 7 kpc, the radio images resolve an elongated ~80 arcsec (2.7 pc) cometary nebula, indicative of a high velocity pulsar. An X-ray counterpart extending ~50 arcsec (1.7 pc) is detected in archival XMM-Newton data. The flat radio spectrum ($α$ = -0.27 $\pm$ 0.05) and hard X-ray photon index ($Γ$ = 1.6 $\pm$ 0.4) indicate synchrotron emission from relativistic particles injected in the pulsar wind. Polarisation analysis reveals a highly ordered magnetic field aligned with the nebular flow, with fractional polarisation reaching up to 30% in the tail. An equipartition estimate gives a PWN magnetic-field strength of Beq $\approx$ 54-140 $μ$G. Pulsar timing over a ~2.2 yr baseline reveals strong timing noise and a small spin glitch with amplitude $Δν/ν$ = 1.10$\times$10$^{-8}$. The SNR shows no clear diffuse X-ray counterpart. The morphology and multiwavelength properties of the Nimbus-Thunder system, along with evolutionary models, constrain the system's age to approximately 30-45 kyr, placing the remnant in the late Sedov phase, approaching the transition to the radiative stage.

AI.tldr: The study reports the discovery and detailed multiwavelength characterization of the Thunder bow-shock pulsar wind nebula powered by PSR J1631-4722 inside the SNR G336.7+0.5 (Nimbus), revealing its morphology, emission properties, magnetic field structure, timing noise, and evolutionary stage around 30-45 kyr old.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize a newly discovered bow-shock pulsar wind nebula associated with a radio pulsar within a Galactic supernova remnant, and to understand its properties and evolutionary state.
AI.method: Multiwavelength observations including radio data from ASKAP EMU survey, MeerKAT Galactic Plane Survey, follow-up ATCA observations at 5.5 and 9 GHz, archival XMM-Newton X-ray data, and pulsar timing analysis over a 2.2-year baseline were employed to study morphology, spectral characteristics, polarization, magnetic field, and timing behavior.
AI.result: Discovery of the Thunder PWN powered by PSR J1631-4722 within SNR G336.7+0.5; resolved elongated nebula indicating high-velocity pulsar; detection of X-ray counterpart; flat radio spectrum and hard X-ray spectrum confirming synchrotron emission; highly ordered magnetic field aligned with nebular flow with up to 30% fractional polarization; magnetic field strength estimated at 54-140 μG; pulsar exhibits strong timing noise and a small spin glitch; SNR lacks clear diffuse X-ray emission; system age constrained to 30-45 kyr in late Sedov phase.
AI.conclusion: The Nimbus-Thunder system is a late Sedov phase supernova remnant with a high-velocity pulsar powering a bow-shock pulsar wind nebula characterized by synchrotron emission and a highly ordered magnetic field, with its age and evolutionary state well constrained through multiwavelength and timing analyses.

title: DSWIM:Efficient and Stable Deterministic Computation of Warm Inflation Perturbations
comment: 22 pages, 6 figures, 1 table, prepared for submission to JCAP
summary: Warm inflation perturbations are sourced by both thermal and quantum fluctuations and are commonly computed through stochastic realizations of the perturbation equations, as implemented in the publicly available code SWIM. Deterministic formulations based on correlation matrix evolution provide a computationally efficient alternative, but can become numerically ill-conditioned when the perturbation variables evolve over widely different scales. In this work, we extend SWIM by introducing a deterministic module, DSWIM, based on correlation matrix evolution. We introduce a physically motivated scaling matrix transformation derived from the effective Hubble scaling of the perturbation variables. The transformed system preserves the primordial curvature power spectrum exactly while substantially improving the numerical conditioning of the deterministic evolution equations. Using representative warm inflation models, we show that the scaled framework suppresses numerical artifacts, improves the robustness of the deterministic evolution, and yields substantial computational speedups while preserving accuracy. We further show that correlated thermal noise contributions arise naturally through the diffusion matrix structure, resolving previously observed discrepancies between stochastic and deterministic implementations. Our results establish DSWIM as a numerically robust and computationally efficient framework for computing warm inflation scalar perturbations.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the warm inflation perturbation code SWIM by developing DSWIM, a deterministic method with a novel scaling transformation that improves numerical stability and speed while maintaining accuracy, effectively bridging gaps between deterministic and stochastic calculations.
AI.motivation: Existing deterministic formulations for warm inflation perturbations are computationally efficient but can suffer from numerical ill-conditioning when perturbation variables evolve across widely varying scales; therefore, a more stable and efficient method was required.
AI.method: Introduction of a deterministic module (DSWIM) based on correlation matrix evolution with a scaling matrix transformation derived from effective Hubble scaling to improve numerical conditioning and preserve the primordial curvature power spectrum exactly.
AI.result: The scaled deterministic framework significantly reduces numerical artifacts, enhances robustness and computational speed, and naturally incorporates correlated thermal noise effects, aligning deterministic results with those from stochastic simulations.
AI.conclusion: DSWIM provides a numerically robust and computationally efficient method for calculating warm inflation scalar perturbations, overcoming numerical challenges present in previous deterministic methods and resolving discrepancies with stochastic approaches.

title: Fermi bubbles detected in $\sim$100 TeV neutrinos
summary: The Fermi bubbles have been identified as a collimated bipolar outflow emanating from the Milky-Way center, tracing strong forward shocks which extend $\sim10$ kpc from the Galactic disk, originating from a $\sim10^{56\pm1}$ erg outburst. These shocks are sufficiently strong, extended, and energetic to produce a detectable flux of $\gtrsim 10$ TeV neutrinos, especially in their denser north and east, but early IceCube data were insufficient for identifying the signal. We find that IceCube high-energy starting events (HESE 12-year) correlate with the $\textit{Fermi}$-LAT sky map outside the Galactic plane ($>3σ$). Testing for neutrinos coincident with the bubble shells, localized using $\textit{eROSITA}$ data, we detect ($>4σ$) both bubbles at high ($|b|>30^{\circ}$) latitudes, with a local excess ($>5σ$) mainly in their X-ray bright eastern shells. The signal matches the anticipated secondaries of relativistic ions carrying $\sim 10^{54.5}$ erg (with factor $\sim3$ uncertainty) in each bubble, shock-accelerated to $>$PeV energies. The results verify the strength of the shocks, suggesting an ion acceleration efficiency of order $\sim10\%$. We also present preliminary evidence for neutrinos from the even larger shells of the eROSITA bubbles, which encapsulate their younger Fermi-bubble counterparts, carrying a similar energy and confined by shocks nearly as strong.

AI.tldr: Analysis of 12 years of IceCube data reveals significant high-energy neutrino emission correlated with the Fermi bubbles' shock fronts, confirming strong ion acceleration and efficient particle acceleration in these Galactic center outflows.
AI.motivation: The study aims to investigate high-energy neutrino emissions associated with the Fermi bubbles, large-scale bipolar outflows from the Milky Way center, which are expected to produce detectable neutrino fluxes due to their strong shocks and energetic processes.
AI.method: The authors analyze 12 years of IceCube high-energy starting events (HESE), correlating the neutrino data with $	extit{Fermi}$-LAT gamma-ray sky maps and localizing the bubble shells using $	extit{eROSITA}$ X-ray data. They perform statistical tests of neutrino excess coincident with the bubble regions at high Galactic latitudes.
AI.result: They detect statistically significant neutrino signals correlated with the Fermi bubbles, with over 4σ significance for both bubbles, and a local excess above 5σ in the X-ray bright eastern shells. The neutrino flux corresponds to relativistic ions accelerated to energies above PeV with an inferred acceleration efficiency of about 10%. Preliminary evidence also suggests neutrino emission from the larger eROSITA bubbles surrounding the younger Fermi bubbles.
AI.conclusion: The results confirm that the Fermi bubble shocks are strong and capable of accelerating ions to very high energies, producing detectable high-energy neutrinos. This validates the theoretical expectations of ion acceleration efficiency and shock energetics in the Galactic center outflows.

title: Unifying the Dark Sector with the New Generalized Chaplygin Gas: Observational Constraints
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, 1 table, Matches published version
summary: In light of recent cosmological observations, we examine a generalized Chaplygin gas model with a redshift-dependent exponent as a framework for describing the dark energy and dark matter content of the Universe. Specifically, we treat this fluid as a single unified component and test it against late-time background observational data. We employ Type Ia supernova data, cosmic chronometers, and baryon acoustic oscillations from the second data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. We perform a Bayesian analysis for parameter estimation and compare the model with $Λ$CDM. We find that the generalized Chaplygin gas provides systematically higher values of the combined likelihood; nevertheless, once the larger number of free parameters is taken into account, both the Bayesian evidence and the Akaike Information Criterion suggest that the model is statistically indistinguishable from $Λ$CDM.

AI.tldr: The paper tests a redshift-dependent generalized Chaplygin gas model as a single dark sector fluid against cosmological data and finds similar statistical support to the standard $\Lambda$CDM model despite having more free parameters.
AI.motivation: To explore a unified description of dark energy and dark matter motivated by recent cosmological observations.
AI.method: Modeling the cosmic fluid as a generalized Chaplygin gas with redshift-dependent exponent; testing against late-time observational data including Type Ia supernovae, cosmic chronometers, and baryon acoustic oscillations; Bayesian parameter estimation and model comparison with $\Lambda$CDM using Bayesian evidence and AIC.
AI.result: The generalized Chaplygin gas model yields higher combined likelihood values but, accounting for more free parameters, is statistically indistinguishable from $\Lambda$CDM based on Bayesian evidence and AIC criteria.
AI.conclusion: The generalized Chaplygin gas with a redshift-dependent exponent is a viable alternative unified model for dark energy and dark matter that fits late-time cosmological data comparably to the standard $\Lambda$CDM model but does not significantly outperform it statistically.

title: Unified Mass-Scaled QPO Signatures of Kerr Sen Black Holes from Stellar Mass to Supermassive Sources
summary: In this study, we numerically investigate Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton (BHL) accretion around Kerr-Sen black holes and examine how the charge-related deformation of the spacetime affects the shock-cone morphology, the variation of the mass accretion rate, and the quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO)-like temporal behavior. The relativistic BHL flow is solved numerically in the equatorial plane for two different black hole spin parameters, a = 0.9 M and a = 0.5 M. From the numerically computed mass accretion rate signal, we calculate the power spectral density (PSD) and perform multi-component Lorentzian fits to identify the dominant QPO-like modes excited around the black hole. The results show that the Kerr-Sen deformation shifts the characteristic frequencies, changes the coherence properties of the oscillation modes, and produces near-resonant harmonic structures close to 3:2 and 2:1. By using inverse mass scaling, the numerically computed frequencies are compared with observed QPOs from stellar-mass, intermediate-mass, and supermassive black hole systems. In particular, reasonable agreement between the numerical simulation results and observations is found for the sources GRS 1915+105, IGR J17091-3624, M82 X-1, NGC 5408 X-1, RE J1034+396, 1H 0707-495, and ESO 113-G010. This comparative analysis indicates that Kerr-Sen black hole shock-cone oscillations may provide a unified framework for interpreting timing features over a broad range of black hole masses and may additionally contribute to constraining the mass and spin parameters of sources whose properties are not yet fully established observationally. These findings further imply that combined hydrodynamical and timing diagnostics constitute a promising approach for assessing the extent to which deviations associated with the Kerr-Sen geometry can be empirically distinguished from those of the Kerr spacetime.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically studies relativistic accretion onto Kerr-Sen black holes, revealing that spacetime charge deformations alter QPO frequencies and mode coherence. The findings align well with observed QPOs across a wide range of black hole masses, suggesting Kerr-Sen effects provide a unified explanation and useful constraints for black hole properties.
AI.motivation: To explore how spacetime deformations related to black hole charge in the Kerr-Sen geometry affect accretion flow dynamics and timing properties, aiming to better understand observed quasi-periodic oscillations and constrain black hole characteristics beyond the standard Kerr spacetime.
AI.method: Numerical simulations of relativistic Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion flows in the equatorial plane around Kerr-Sen black holes with two spin parameters (a=0.9M and a=0.5M) were performed. Power spectral density of the mass accretion rate signals was analyzed using multi-component Lorentzian fits to extract dominant QPO-like modes.
AI.result: The Kerr-Sen deformation shifts characteristic oscillation frequencies, alters mode coherence, and produces near-resonant harmonic frequency structures. Numerical frequencies scaled by inverse mass show good agreement with QPO observations across stellar-mass to supermassive black holes. Results suggest that Kerr-Sen shock-cone oscillations can unify timing feature interpretation and aid parameter constraints for various sources.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that Kerr-Sen black hole deformations significantly influence shock-cone morphology, mass accretion rate variability, and QPO-like oscillation properties, providing a potential unified explanation for observed QPOs across diverse black hole masses and helping constrain black hole parameters.

title: Revisiting the 'Lensing is Low' Problem with UNIONS
comment: 21 article pages, 19 figures, submitted to MNRAS
summary: We present new measurements of the galaxy-galaxy lensing (GGL) signal around Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (BOSS) CMASS galaxies using background sources from the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS). With high-quality imaging of background sources and a survey overlap of approximately 2650 square degrees, we obtain precise large-scale GGL measurements. Building on these new measurements, we revisit the so-called 'lensing is low' problem, wherein galaxy-halo connection models calibrated on galaxy clustering (GC) data over-predict the GGL signal by 20-40% assuming CMB-based cosmological parameters. We model the galaxy-halo connection using a halo occupation distribution (HOD), and perform joint fits to both GGL and GC signals across a wide range of scales, as well as a GC-only fit. In contrast to previous work, we do not find a significant 'lensing is low' effect in the CMASS sample, although the best joint fits are achieved by decreasing the amplitude of the matter power spectrum slightly relative to the Planck cosmological parameters. Overall, we find that two models describe our observables similarly well: one where HOD and cosmological parameters are free, and one where HOD, cosmological, and feedback parameters are free. Importantly, we emphasise the role of large scales in constraining the lensing is low effect, shifting the narrative away from an exclusively small-scale issue.

AI.tldr: New precise galaxy-galaxy lensing measurements with UNIONS data show no strong 'lensing is low' problem in BOSS CMASS galaxies; joint galaxy-halo and cosmology modeling suggests large scales are essential to resolving previous tensions.
AI.motivation: To address the discrepancy known as the 'lensing is low' problem where galaxy-halo models over-predict galaxy-galaxy lensing signals compared to clustering data under standard cosmology.
AI.method: New precise galaxy-galaxy lensing measurements from UNIONS around BOSS CMASS galaxies, halo occupation distribution modeling, and joint fitting to both lensing and clustering data across multiple scales.
AI.result: No significant 'lensing is low' effect detected in the CMASS sample; best fits require a slight decrease in matter power spectrum amplitude relative to Planck cosmology; both cosmological and feedback parameter-inclusive models fit data similarly well.
AI.conclusion: The 'lensing is low' tension is not strongly supported by new large-scale precise measurements; large scales play a crucial role in constraining the effect, moving the discussion beyond a small-scale-only issue.

title: Polarization Angle Geodesics in PSRs B1133+16 and B2016+28
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ; 33 pages and 11 figures
summary: Recent models of pulsar polarization predict that the position and ellipticity angles of the polarization vector can trace portions of a small or great circle on the Poincare sphere. A great circle can arise from a transition in dominance of orthogonal polarization modes, where the relative intensity of the modes changes with pulse longitude. A small circle may be caused by a rotation of the vector, where the phase difference between the modes changes with pulse longitude or wavelength. Observations of PSRs B1133+16 and B2016+28 are reanalyzed to search for these polarization features within their pulse profiles. The polarization angles observed in part of PSR B1133+16 are shown to follow a great circle on the Poincare sphere. The angles observed across the pulse of PSR B2016+28 follow an arc that resembles a portion of a great circle that has been altered by the pulsar's rotation. The observations are interpreted within the context of three different polarization models. All three models produce similar results for both pulsars and indicate that the observed geodesics are caused by mode transitions. The arc observed in PSR B2016+28 can also be interpreted as a vector rotation, provided the modes are elliptically polarized. The observations and accompanying analysis show that mode transitions are not restricted to the equatorial plane of the Poincare sphere and that arcs and partial circles may be more common than previously recognized.

AI.tldr: Polarization vectors in pulsars PSR B1133+16 and B2016+28 trace great or small circles on the Poincare sphere due to orthogonal mode transitions and vector rotations, revealing that such polarization features are common beyond the previously assumed equatorial plane limitation.
AI.motivation: To investigate the polarization behavior of pulsars and understand the geometric nature of polarization vector trajectories on the Poincare sphere, especially focusing on mode transitions and vector rotations.
AI.method: Reanalysis of polarization angle data from pulse profiles of PSRs B1133+16 and B2016+28 using three different polarization models, examining their trajectories on the Poincare sphere.
AI.result: Both pulsars show polarization angles tracing geodesics on the Poincare sphere: PSR B1133+16 follows a great circle, while PSR B2016+28 follows an arc resembling a great circle modified by rotation. The results suggest mode transitions are responsible and can occur off the equatorial plane, with mode vectors possibly elliptically polarized.
AI.conclusion: Mode transitions in pulsar polarization are more geometrically varied than previously thought, involving great and small circle trajectories not confined to the equatorial plane of the Poincare sphere, indicating more common occurrence of arcs and partial circles in polarization data.

title: UHECR Clustering: Lightest Nuclei from Local Sheet Galaxies
summary: The ultra-high-energy cosmic ray (UHECR) puzzle is reviewed under the hints of a few basic results: clustering, anisotropy, asymmetry, bending, and composition changes with energies. We show how the lightest UHECR nuclei from the nearest AGN or Star-Burst sources, located inside a few Mpc Local Sheets, may explain, at best, the observed clustering of Hot Spots at tens EeV energy. Among the possible local extragalactic candidate sources, we derived the main contribution of very few galactic sources. These are located in the Local Sheet plane within a distance of a few Mpc, ejecting UHECR at a few tens of EeV energy. UHECR also shine at lower energies of several EeV, partially feeding the Auger dipole by LMC and possibly a few nearer galactic sources. For the very recent highest energy UHECR event, if a nucleon, it may be explained by a model based on the scattering of UHE ZeV neutrinos on low-mass relic neutrinos. Such scatterings are capable of correlating, via Z boson resonance, the most distant cosmic sources above the GZK bound with such an enigmatic UHECR event. Otherwise, these extreme events, if made by the heaviest composition, could originate from the largest bending trajectory of heaviest nuclei or from nearby sources, even galactic ones. In summary, the present lightest to heavy nuclei model UHECR from the Local Sheet could successfully correlate UHECR clustering with the nearest galaxies and AGN. Heavy UHECR may shine by being widely deflected from the Local Sheet or from past galactic, GRB, or SGR explosive ejection.

AI.tldr: UHECR clustering and anisotropy are best explained by a model where lightest nuclei originate from nearby extragalactic sources in the Local Sheet, with contributions from a few galactic sources. Extreme energy events may arise from ZeV neutrino interactions or heavy nuclei from local sources.
AI.motivation: To address and explain the puzzle of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECR) observed clustering, anisotropy, composition changes, and their origin.
AI.method: Analysis of UHECR clustering, anisotropy, and composition data, with modeling of lightest to heaviest nuclei sources within a few Mpc Local Sheet, including nearby AGN, star-burst sources, and galactic contributions. Consideration of nucleon models involving ZeV neutrino scattering for extreme energy events.
AI.result: The model suggests that lightest UHECR nuclei from nearby extragalactic sources within the Local Sheet explain clustering at tens of EeV energies. A few galactic sources contribute to lower energy UHECR and dipole anisotropy. Extreme energy events may be explained by either ZeV neutrino scattering or heavy nuclei with large deflection trajectories from nearby or galactic sources.
AI.conclusion: UHECR observations, including clustering and composition changes, can be effectively correlated with sources located within the Local Sheet at a few Mpc distance. Both light and heavy nuclei models are necessary to explain the full range of UHECR phenomena, with local extragalactic and galactic sources contributing to observed patterns.

title: Finite-volume scheme for first-order viscoresistive relativistic magnetohydrodynamics
summary: We present a numerical implementation of dissipative relativistic magnetohydrodynamics based on Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) theory, in which first-order corrections render the equations causal without introducing additional dynamical variables. We show how these corrections can be incorporated in a finite-volume scheme describing the coupled dissipation of energy, momentum, and magnetic field, with the latter treated as a one-form charge. While a minimal set of BDNK terms can convert diffusive equations into telegrapher-type equations, we find that in the ultra-relativistic limit an additional correction is required for the system to behave in a stable and causal manner. With this set of equations, we develop an efficient method for primitive-variable recovery and validate the implementation through an analytical benchmark and various two-dimensional simulations.

AI.tldr: Introduces a stable, causal numerical scheme for dissipative relativistic magnetohydrodynamics using BDNK theory, validated through benchmarks and 2D simulations, with novel corrections for ultra-relativistic stability.
AI.motivation: To develop a relativistic magnetohydrodynamics model that remains causal and stable by incorporating dissipative effects without adding additional dynamical variables.
AI.method: Numerical implementation of dissipative relativistic magnetohydrodynamics based on Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) theory utilizing a finite-volume scheme and treating magnetic fields as one-form charges; development of an efficient primitive-variable recovery method.
AI.result: Demonstration that a minimal set of BDNK terms transforms diffusive to telegrapher-type equations, and identification of an additional correction needed for ultra-relativistic stable, causal behavior; successful validation against analytical benchmarks and 2D simulations.
AI.conclusion: The BDNK-based numerical framework effectively models dissipative relativistic magnetohydrodynamics with stable and causal dynamics, including necessary corrections for ultra-relativistic regimes, and enables efficient and accurate simulations.

title: Testing the Generalization and Domain Stability of Compact Feature Representations for Photometric Supernova Classification
comment: 13 pages, 4 figures, 10 tables. Submitted to the Journal of Astrophysics and Astronomy
summary:
Photometric classification of supernovae increasingly requires models that are not only accurate within a single survey but also robust to changes in cadence, noise properties, filter coverage, and survey domain. We investigate the generalization and domain stability of a compact 16-feature representation for Type Ia supernova classification. The feature set consists of physically interpretable descriptors of brightness, color, variability, and temporal evolution. Using the Supernova Photometric Classification Challenge (SPCC) dataset as the reference domain, we confirm that a compact XGBoost classifier achieves strong within-survey performance, reaching an F1 score of 0.844 and a PR-AUC of 0.928 on a held-out test set. We then evaluate robustness under alternative classifiers, repeated resampling, feature perturbations, missing-band proxies, shortened temporal coverage, and cross-survey transfer to PLAsTiCC.
  The compact representation remains stable under resampling and moderate perturbations, but direct SPCC$\rightarrow$PLAsTiCC transfer produces a substantial performance degradation. Class-conditional centroid analysis shows that the SPCC and PLAsTiCC Type Ia populations occupy different regions of the compact feature space. The cross-survey Ia centroid shift exceeds the Ia/non-Ia separation within either survey, indicating that the transfer gap is driven primarily by feature-space domain shift rather than classifier instability. These results show that compact physically interpretable features are robust within a survey and useful for diagnostic analysis, but are not automatically survey-invariant. Cross-survey deployment therefore requires feature harmonization, domain adaptation, or restriction to a smaller set of survey-stable features.

AI.tldr: A compact 16-feature physically interpretable model classifies Type Ia supernovae well within a single survey but suffers performance loss when transferred across surveys due to domain shifts, highlighting the need for domain adaptation or harmonization in cross-survey applications.
AI.motivation: To develop supernova classification models that are not only accurate within a single survey but also robust across different survey conditions such as cadence, noise, filter coverage, and domain shifts.
AI.method: Constructed a compact 16-feature physically interpretable representation for Type Ia supernova classification, using descriptors of brightness, color, variability, and temporal evolution. Evaluated model robustness using XGBoost classifiers on SPCC and cross-survey transfer to PLAsTiCC with analyses including resampling, feature perturbations, missing data proxies, and centroid shifts.
AI.result: The compact 16-feature representation achieved strong within-survey classification performance (F1=0.844, PR-AUC=0.928) and remained stable under resampling and perturbations. However, cross-survey transfer (SPCC to PLAsTiCC) showed substantial performance degradation due to domain shifts in the feature space rather than classifier instability.
AI.conclusion: Compact, physically interpretable supernova features offer robust and diagnostically useful classification within a survey, but are not inherently invariant across different surveys. Successful cross-survey classification requires feature harmonization, domain adaptation, or limiting features to those stable across surveys.

title: Are most detected tidal disruption events partial?
summary: During a tidal disruption event (TDE), a star loses mass due to the tidal gravitational forces of the black hole. In a partial tidal disruption event, a stellar remnant is left behind. Several dozen TDEs have been detected so far, including repeating partial events. We use the Phantom smoothed particle hydrodynamics code to model the disruption of a 1 Msun star around a 10^6 Msun black hole for impact parameters resulting in less than equal to 50 % mass loss. We only consider zero energy orbits. Our simulations show that the mass fallback rate can exceed the Eddington limit for beta greater than or equal to 0.8, allowing debris to obscure the accretion disc by forming a reprocessing layer, similar to full TDEs. The mass fallback rate is shallower than t^{-5/3}, tracking closer to t^{-9/4}. Assuming thermal emission from the debris, that shock heating is trapped, that electron scattering dominates the opacity, and a color correction f_{col} of 1.7, we find temperatures of ~10^4 K, optical bolometric luminosities of ~ 10^{42-44} erg/s and blackbody radii ranging from 10-100 au for our simulations. We compare our values with observations and find support for the previous argument that some TDEs classified as full disruptions might actually be partial. Moreover, our results explain the detected optical/UV TDEs. We also find that our zero energy partial TDEs have properties similar to the repeating partial TDEs such as ASSASN-19dj, ASSASN-14ko, ASSASN-18ul, ASSASN-22ci, AT2020vdq and AT2022dbl. In the beta=0.8, isentropic simulation where radiation is assumed to escape, we find X-ray luminosities of ~ 10^{44-45} erg/s and radii lower than the inner most stable circular orbit.

AI.tldr: Simulations of partial tidal disruption events of a solar mass star by a supermassive black hole show fallback rates exceeding Eddington limits and optical/X-ray emissions matching observations, indicating some full TDEs may actually be partial disruptions.
AI.motivation: To better understand the dynamics and observational signatures of partial tidal disruption events (TDEs) where a stellar remnant remains after partial mass loss.
AI.method: Used Phantom smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations to model the disruption of a 1 solar mass star around a 10^6 solar mass black hole under zero energy orbits with impact parameters causing up to 50% mass loss.
AI.result: Mass fallback rates exceed the Eddington limit for beta ≥ 0.8 and follow a shallower decay (~t^{-9/4}) than classical predictions; the simulations predict optical/UV temperatures around 10^4 K, luminosities 10^{42-44} erg/s, and blackbody radii from 10-100 au. Simulated properties align with some observed repeat partial TDEs and suggest some events classified as full disruptions may be partial. Simulations assuming radiation escape yield X-ray luminosities of 10^{44-45} erg/s with inner radii smaller than the ISCO.
AI.conclusion: Partial TDEs under zero energy orbits can produce observable signatures similar to full disruptions, explaining observed optical/UV emission and repeating partial TDE events; the fallback rate deviates from classical theory and can exceed Eddington luminosities, potentially leading to obscuration of the accretion disk.

title: On the assessment of the disk truncation and detection of type-II bursts from the accreting millisecond X-ray Pulsar IGR J17062-6143
comment: 29 pages, 8 figures and 6 tables, submitted to Journal of High Energy Astrophysics
summary: We present a spectral analysis of the NuSTAR and NICER observations of the accreting millisecond X-ray pulsar IGR J17062-6143, performed in 2022. The source remained in the hard spectral state during the observations, with a luminosity of about 0.2-1.3$\%$ of the Eddington luminosity. The continuum emission of the NuSTAR spectrum is entirely dominated by a power-law component or by Comptonized emission of disk photons by a plasma with a high electron temperature ($\gtrsim100$ keV). The NuSTAR spectrum also reveals clear evidence of disk reflection, a broad Fe K line around 6-8 keV, and a Compton hump peaking at 20 keV, irrespective of the choice of the continuum models. Our spectral studies suggest a disk extending close to the neutron star surface ($\sim$7-17 $R_{\rm g}$) at low inclination angles ($\sim$20$^\circ$-40$^\circ$), as revealed by a couple of self-consistent relativistic reflection models, relxill and relxillCP. In addition, we detected type-II bursts for the first time in the NICER observation of this source. Light curve profiles of type-II bursts exhibit different patterns, mostly associated with the so-called mode-0 and mode-1 type-II bursts. The energy spectra of the persistent (pre-burst) and burst emission are well described by an absorbed Comptonization component, scattering diskbb- and blackbody-distributed photons, respectively, by a corona with a temperature of 1-3 keV. Although the origin of the type-II burst is not very clear, it has been substantially linked to magnetospheric gating of the accretion flow.

AI.tldr: This study analyzed NuSTAR and NICER data of IGR J17062-6143 in 2022, finding a hard spectral state with high-temperature Comptonized emission and disk reflection near the neutron star. For the first time, type-II bursts were detected and modeled, likely caused by magnetospheric gating of the accretion.
AI.motivation: To understand the spectral properties and burst behavior of the accreting millisecond X-ray pulsar IGR J17062-6143 during a low-luminosity hard state.
AI.method: Performed spectral analysis of NuSTAR and NICER X-ray observations using continuum fitting and relativistic reflection models (relxill and relxillCP) and studied timing properties of type-II bursts.
AI.result: The source was in a hard spectral state with luminosity at 0.2-1.3% of Eddington. The spectrum shows a power-law or Comptonized emission with high electron temperature (>100 keV), disk reflection features including a broad Fe K line and Compton hump, and suggests a disk extending close to the neutron star at low inclination. NICER observations detected type-II bursts exhibiting mode-0 and mode-1 patterns. Persistent and burst spectra fitted by absorbed Comptonization with a 1-3 keV corona. Type-II bursts likely linked to magnetospheric gating of accretion.
AI.conclusion: IGR J17062-6143 remained in a hard spectral state during the 2022 observations with emission dominated by Comptonized disk photons and clear disk reflection signatures. The inner accretion disk extends close to the neutron star surface at low inclination. The detection and characterization of type-II bursts suggest a magnetospheric origin affecting the accretion flow.

title: When the black holes align: a subpopulation of aligned massive binary black holes observed via gravitational waves
summary: In this work, we investigate the features present in the joint primary mass and effective spin distribution of binary black holes without relying on specific modelling assumptions. We make use of non-parametric methods, flexible models capable of approximating arbitrary probability densities with minimal mathematical assumptions, applying it to the newly released GWTC-5.0. Our analysis supports the presence of at least two separate sub-population of binary black holes showing different effective spin distributions: one of them, preferring positive $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ values, points towards the direction of systems formed in a non-spherically-symmetric, dynamical environment.

AI.tldr: Using non-parametric analysis on GWTC-5.0 data, this study reveals at least two distinct sub-populations of binary black holes differentiated by their effective spin distributions, one indicative of dynamic, non-spherically symmetric formation.
AI.motivation: To understand the underlying features in the distribution of primary mass and effective spin of binary black holes without imposing restrictive modeling assumptions.
AI.method: Non-parametric methods and flexible models were employed to analyze the joint distribution of primary mass and effective spin of binary black holes, applied to data from the GWTC-5.0 catalog without relying on specific modelling assumptions.
AI.result: Identification of at least two separate sub-populations of binary black holes with distinct effective spin distributions, notably one sub-population preferring positive effective spin values suggesting a dynamic formation environment.
AI.conclusion: There exist at least two distinct sub-populations of binary black holes characterized by different effective spin distributions, one showing a preference for positive effective spins indicative of formation in non-spherically-symmetric, dynamical environments.

title: Galactic Cosmic Ray Transport in the Giant Circumgalactic Medium Halo
summary: Recent observations have revealed that the Milky Way is embedded in a massive circumgalactic medium (CGM) extending to several hundred kiloparsecs. Such an extended gaseous halo acts as both a reservoir of baryons and potentially as a confinement volume for Galactic cosmic rays (CRs). We investigate CR transport in this giant Galactic halo and compare its properties with those of conventional small-halo models. In the giant-halo scenario, the halo height is no longer a free parameter, but instead relates to the extent of the source region. We show that CR transport within the source region remains similar to that in small-halo models, while substantial differences emerge at larger distances. In the giant-halo scenario, CRs develop an extended approximately 1/r spatial tail and exhibit a broader age distribution than the small-halo case. This model is shown to be consistent with current secondary-to-primary CR measurements. We further find that uncertainties associated with Galactic gas distributions are comparable to those arising from nuclear spallation cross sections. These results suggest that the giant-halo model provides a physically motivated alternative to conventional small-halo models and may have important implications for diffuse gamma-ray and neutrino emission from the Galactic environment.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates cosmic ray transport in the Milky Way's large circumgalactic medium, showing that the giant-halo model, which ties halo size to source extent, predicts extended cosmic ray distributions consistent with observed data, and challenges conventional small-halo models, with consequences for gamma-ray and neutrino astronomy.
