AI.motivation: The study aims to understand cosmic ray transport in the massive circumgalactic medium (CGM) surrounding the Milky Way, motivated by recent observations indicating the presence of a large gaseous halo extending several hundred kiloparsecs, which may serve as a cosmic ray confinement volume.
AI.method: The authors compare cosmic ray transport properties between the giant-halo model—which links halo height to the extent of the source region—and conventional small-halo models, analyzing spatial distribution and age profiles of cosmic rays and assessing consistency with secondary-to-primary cosmic ray measurements, while considering uncertainties in Galactic gas distributions and nuclear spallation cross sections.
AI.result: The giant-halo model results in cosmic rays developing an extended roughly 1/r spatial tail and a broader age distribution compared to small-halo models, remaining consistent with current secondary-to-primary cosmic ray data. Uncertainties from Galactic gas distributions are found to be as significant as those from nuclear spallation cross sections. This supports the giant-halo model as a physically motivated alternative to small-halo models with implications for understanding diffuse gamma-ray and neutrino emissions.
AI.conclusion: The giant-halo model is a viable, physically motivated framework for cosmic ray transport in the Milky Way, offering an alternative to small-halo models by incorporating an extensive circumgalactic medium, and has potential implications for interpreting diffuse gamma-ray and neutrino emission from the Galaxy.

title: Reverberation in the Narrow Fe K$α$ Line in the Seyfert Galaxy NGC 4151 with XRISM
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ Letters
summary: Emission lines that "echo" variations in the ionizing flux produced close to black holes are powerful probes of the central engine. In the Seyfert-1.5 galaxy NGC 4151, high-resolution X-ray spectra and time lags in low-resolution X-ray data suggest that part of the narrow Fe K$_α$ line originates close to the optical broad line region (BLR). We report on a sequence of nine XRISM observations of NGC 4151, obtained every other day in 2024. Swift monitoring was undertaken to sample the driving flux before, during, and after the XRISM sequence. Using suitable line kernels, we measure a mean BLR component width of $σ= 5.36\pm 0.48\times 10^{3}~{\rm km}~ {\rm s}^{-1}$. Modeling the Swift continuum and XRISM line flux trends gives a lag of $τ= 3.5^{+2.8}_{-1.7}$ days ($r=3.6^{+3.0}_{-1.7}\times 10^{3}~GM/c^{2}$ for $M_{BH} = 1.7\times 10^{7}~M_{\odot}$), significant at the $2σ$ level via Monte Carlo simulations, and consistent with prior measurements and direct spectral fits. This lag implies a black hole mass of $M_{BH}/f_{X} = 2.0^{+1.4}_{-1.0}\times 10^{7} M_{\odot}$, where $f_{X}$ is a geometrical factor. A standard optical value for this factor gives a mass that is nominally higher than typical H$β$ mass estimates, but formally consistent. Our results suggest that XRISM can measure lags and black hole masses in both unobscured and obscured AGN.

AI.tldr: This study uses nine XRISM X-ray observations and Swift monitoring of NGC 4151 to measure the broad line region size and black hole mass via X-ray emission line time lags, confirming XRISM's capability to probe black hole environments in AGN.
AI.motivation: To use emission lines that echo ionizing flux variations near black holes as probes to better understand the central engine in AGN, specifically in NGC 4151.
AI.method: A sequence of nine XRISM X-ray observations of NGC 4151 spaced every two days was conducted along with Swift monitoring to sample the driving flux. Line kernels were applied to measure the broad line region width and model flux trends to determine time lags and estimate black hole mass.
AI.result: Measured a BLR component width of σ = 5.36 ± 0.48 × 10^3 km/s, a time lag of 3.5^{+2.8}_{-1.7} days significant at 2σ level, and a black hole mass estimate of M_BH/f_X = 2.0^{+1.4}_{-1.0} × 10^7 M_⊙, consistent with prior measurements and optical mass values within uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: XRISM observations can effectively measure X-ray emission line lags and black hole masses in both unobscured and obscured active galactic nuclei, providing valuable constraints on the structure and dynamics near supermassive black holes.

title: Neutron Star Mass-Radius Constraints for EXO 0748$-$676 from 2008-2025 Quiescent X-ray Spectra
summary: We present new constraints on the mass and radius of the neutron star in the neutron star low-mass X-ray binary EXO 0748$-$676 obtained from a joint analysis of 20 quiescent X-ray observations obtained between 2008 and 2025, including 14 Chandra and 6 XMM-Newton exposures. These data sample two quiescent episodes separated by the 2024$-$2025 outburst. We model the 0.5$-$10 keV spectra with a hydrogen-atmosphere model, assuming a source distance of 7.1 kpc. In a global Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis in which the hydrogen column density, neutron star mass, and radius are tied across all observations, we obtain a neutron-star mass of $1.77^{+0.17}_{-0.22}\,M_\odot$ and a radius of $12.62^{+0.56}_{-0.74}$ km ($1σ$ credible intervals). We further perform independent fits to the first and second quiescent epochs and find that the combined data set significantly reduces the low-mass tail in the posterior distribution, leading to tighter lower bounds on the neutron-star mass. Incorporating the distance uncertainty of $7.1\pm1.2$ kpc, we conservatively constrain the neutron-star mass and radius to $M\simeq 1.41-2.11~M_{\odot}$ and $R\simeq 10.15-15.13$ km, favoring relatively stiff dense-matter equations of state. We also trace the thermal evolution across two quiescent epochs and find evidence for renewed crust cooling following the 2024$-$2025 outburst, providing a unique opportunity to compare the thermal relaxation behavior after two distinct accretion episodes.

AI.tldr: This study uses 20 quiescent X-ray observations of EXO 0748−676 across two epochs to jointly constrain its neutron star mass and radius, favoring stiff dense matter equations of state and observing crust cooling evolution after recent outbursts.
AI.motivation: To refine constraints on neutron star mass and radius using extensive quiescent X-ray observational data of EXO 0748−676, critical for dense matter equation of state studies.
AI.method: Joint spectral modeling of 20 quiescent X-ray observations from Chandra and XMM-Newton over two epochs using hydrogen-atmosphere models and a global Markov Chain Monte Carlo framework tying hydrogen column density, mass, and radius.
AI.result: Neutron star mass constrained to 1.77+0.17−0.22 M⊙ and radius to 12.62+0.56−0.74 km (1σ), with conservative ranges accounting for distance uncertainty as 1.41–2.11 M⊙ and 10.15–15.13 km; data favor stiff dense-matter equations of state and reveal renewed crust cooling post 2024–2025 outburst.
AI.conclusion: Combined multi-epoch X-ray spectral analysis significantly tightens neutron star mass and radius constraints, reducing low-mass posterior tail, and demonstrates crust cooling evolution after multiple accretion episodes in EXO 0748−676.

title: TeV-PeV Gamma-ray and Neutrino Emission in the Galactic Plane
comment: 11 pages, 7 figures, accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: We model the LHAASO observation of diffuse TeV--PeV $γ$ rays in the Galactic plane as the sum of unresolved leptonic emission from pulsar wind nebulae and hadronic emission from supernova-injected cosmic-ray (CR) protons. We investigate uncertainties in the radial distribution of the infrared component of the interstellar radiation field (ISRF), using profiles with enhanced photon densities in the inner Galaxy. We quantify their effects on $γγ$ attenuation of the diffuse $γ$-ray emission. The alternative ISRF models affect the LHAASO diffuse fit only modestly, as the analysis excludes the Galactic center direction and applies source masks in the Galactic plane. Using the hadronic normalization inferred from the LHAASO fit for various ISRF models, the associated $pp$ neutrino emission remains consistent with the IceCube all-sky measurement, while the flux from the Galactic Ridge region remains compatible with current ANTARES and KM3NeT constraints. Since the modified infrared profiles differ most strongly toward the inner Galaxy, we also examine their impact on inverse-Compton emission from point sources near the central molecular zone. These same models can noticeably modify the hadronic and inverse-Compton $γ$-ray emission above $\sim\!10$ TeV from sources in the central region. Future KM3NeT observations, combined with $γ$-ray measurements of individual sources, can probe the inner-Galaxy CR population and constrain the radial distribution of the ISRF near the Galactic Center.

AI.tldr: This paper models diffuse TeV-PeV gamma-rays in the Galactic plane considering uncertainties in the infrared ISRF, finds that these uncertainties slightly affect gamma-ray fits and neutrino emission predictions, and highlights that future observations can constrain the inner Galaxy's cosmic-ray and ISRF properties.
AI.motivation: To understand how uncertainties in the infrared component of the ISRF, particularly in the inner Galaxy, affect modeling of diffuse high-energy gamma-ray emission and its attenuation, and to assess implications for associated neutrino emission and cosmic-ray population studies near the Galactic Center.
AI.method: The paper models diffuse TeV-PeV gamma-ray observations as a combination of leptonic emission from pulsar wind nebulae and hadronic emission from cosmic-ray protons injected by supernovae. It investigates different radial profiles of the infrared ISRF component, assessing their influence on gamma-gamma attenuation and gamma-ray fits to LHAASO data, excluding the Galactic center direction and applying source masks. Hadronic normalization is derived from fits for each ISRF model to predict associated neutrino emissions, compared with IceCube, ANTARES, and KM3NeT data. The study also examines inverse-Compton gamma-ray emission near the Galactic Center under alternative ISRF models.
AI.result: Alternative ISRF models show modest effects on diffuse gamma-ray fits excluding the Galactic center, keep predicted neutrino emissions consistent with current measurements, and visibly alter high-energy gamma-ray emission from sources near the central molecular zone. These findings suggest that future KM3NeT neutrino observations and gamma-ray measurements can help probe and constrain the inner Galaxy's cosmic-ray population and the radial ISRF distribution.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that variations in the radial distribution of the infrared component of the ISRF moderately affect the modeling of diffuse gamma-ray emission in the Galactic plane, without significantly altering neutrino emission predictions consistent with IceCube, ANTARES, and KM3NeT data. It also finds that these ISRF variations have a notable impact on high-energy gamma-ray emission from sources near the Galactic Center, suggesting future observations could further constrain ISRF properties and cosmic-ray populations in that region.

title: A Tentative Double Excess in the Gamma-Ray Spectrum of the Fermi Blazar 4FGL J0604.9-0000
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, 1 table, Comments are welcome!
summary: Based on 17.75 years of Fermi-LAT observations, we report a tentative double excess in the gamma-ray spectrum of the blazar 4FGL J0604.9-0000, with peak energies at approximately 1.5 GeV and 11 GeV. The two excesses are modeled as double Gaussian components. For the lower-energy excess, the best-fit centroid is $E_1 = 1.59\pm0.07$ GeV with a width fixed to the instrumental resolution ($σ_1 = 0.145$ GeV). For the higher-energy excess, the centroid is $E_2 = 11.15\pm0.61$ GeV and the width is constrained to $σ_2 = 1.185$ GeV (about 10\% of the peak energy), which is comparable to the Fermi-LAT energy resolution at that energy. The two features have local significances of $2.6σ$ and $3.7σ$ (3 dof), respectively. A joint likelihood analysis yields a combined test statistic of TS $\simeq 27$, corresponding to a local significance of approximately $4.3σ$ (4 dof, without correction for trials and the look-elsewhere effect) or about $4.8σ$ (2 dof). To our knowledge, no other active galactic nucleus has been reported to show a similar double-excess candidate. The observed energy ratio of $\sim$1:7 is difficult to explain with standard astrophysical emission processes. However, the energies and their ratio are consistent with dark matter annihilation (e.g., $χχ\toγγ$ and $χχ\toγγ'$) for a particle mass near 11 GeV, making this source a promising target for follow-up observations with next-generation gamma-ray telescopes.

AI.tldr: A detailed 17.75-year Fermi-LAT study of blazar 4FGL J0604.9-0000 reveals a unique double gamma-ray excess at ~1.5 GeV and ~11 GeV, potentially indicating dark matter annihilation, warranting further observational follow-up.
AI.motivation: To investigate unusual features in the gamma-ray spectrum of the blazar 4FGL J0604.9-0000 over a long observation period, potentially revealing new astrophysical phenomena or dark matter signals.
AI.method: Long-term analysis of 17.75 years of Fermi-LAT gamma-ray data, modeling the spectrum with double Gaussian components, and performing a joint likelihood analysis to evaluate the significance of observed excesses.
AI.result: Identification of two tentative gamma-ray excesses at ~1.5 GeV and ~11 GeV with local significances of 2.6σ and 3.7σ respectively, combined to a ~4.3-4.8σ significance, featuring an energy ratio (~1:7) inconsistent with common astrophysical emissions but consistent with signals expected from dark matter annihilation.
AI.conclusion: The blazar 4FGL J0604.9-0000 exhibits a unique double gamma-ray excess possibly linked to dark matter annihilation signatures, making it a promising candidate for future gamma-ray observations to confirm this tentative discovery.

title: Spectral and timing variability of the transient ultraluminous X-ray source NGC 4631 X-4
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)
summary: Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) are among the best laboratories for studying super-Eddington accretion onto compact objects. We present a detailed spectral and timing analysis of the transient ULX NGC 4631 X-4 using archival Chandra, XMM-Newton, and Swift/XRT observations. The source exhibits pronounced spectral and flux variability on both short and long timescales, with luminosity variations exceeding two orders of magnitude. Its X-ray spectra are well described by absorbed multicolor disk blackbody and power-law models, with characteristic inner disk temperatures of 0.9-1.4 keV and photon indices of 2.0-2.4. The source does not follow the standard luminosity-temperature relation expected for a geometrically thin, optically thick accretion disk. No coherent pulsations or quasi-periodic oscillations are detected, while the short-term variability is dominated by aperiodic fluctuations and kilosecond peak-like structures, consistent with clumpy winds and geometric effects in a super-Eddington accretion flow. Overall, the spectral and timing properties support super-Eddington accretion onto a stellar-mass compact object, although the current data do not allow us to distinguish uniquely between a neutron star and a stellar-mass black hole accretor.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes the transient ULX NGC 4631 X-4, revealing spectral and timing features consistent with super-Eddington accretion onto a stellar-mass compact object, but cannot conclusively distinguish between a neutron star or black hole accretor.
AI.motivation: To investigate the nature of super-Eddington accretion processes in ultraluminous X-ray sources by studying the transient ULX NGC 4631 X-4, which exhibits significant spectral and flux variability.
AI.method: A detailed spectral and timing analysis was performed using archival data from Chandra, XMM-Newton, and Swift/XRT, applying absorbed multicolor disk blackbody and power-law spectral models, and examining variability on multiple timescales.
AI.result: The source exhibits large luminosity variations (over two orders of magnitude), inconsistent luminosity-temperature relations for standard thin disks, absence of coherent pulsations or QPOs, and timing features indicating clumpy winds and geometric effects, consistent with super-Eddington accretion onto a stellar-mass compact object.
AI.conclusion: The spectral and timing properties of NGC 4631 X-4 strongly support super-Eddington accretion onto a stellar-mass compact object, but the data do not conclusively identify whether the accretor is a neutron star or a black hole.
